```sql
SELECT 
    p.player_name, 
    SUM(b.bowler_runs) * 1.0 / COUNT(w.wicket_id) AS bowling_average
FROM 
    wicket_taken w
JOIN 
    ball_by_ball b ON w.match_id = b.match_id 
        AND w.inning_no = b.inning_no 
        AND w.over_id = b.over_id 
        AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
JOIN 
    player p ON w.bowler = p.player_id
GROUP BY 
    w.bowler, p.player_name
HAVING 
    COUNT(w.wicket_id) > 0
ORDER BY 
    bowling_average ASC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH monthly_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', transaction_date) AS month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) -
    SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM bitcoin_transactions
  WHERE strftime('%Y', transaction_date) = '2020'
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
),
positive_balance_counts AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS positive_customer_count
  FROM monthly_balance
  WHERE month_end_balance > 0
  GROUP BY month
),
extreme_months AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT month FROM positive_balance_counts ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, month ASC LIMIT 1) AS max_month,
    (SELECT month FROM positive_balance_counts ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, month ASC LIMIT 1) AS min_month
),
avg_balance_per_extreme_month AS (
  SELECT
    mb.month,
    AVG(mb.month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM monthly_balance mb
  JOIN extreme_months em
    ON mb.month = em.max_month OR mb.month = em.min_month
  GROUP BY mb.month
)
SELECT
  em.max_month AS month_with_most_positive_balances,
  em.min_month AS month_with_least_positive_balances,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ab.month = em.max_month THEN ab.avg_balance END) AS avg_balance_max_month,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ab.month = em.min_month THEN ab.avg_balance END) AS avg_balance_min_month,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ab.month = em.max_month THEN ab.avg_balance END) - 
    MAX(CASE WHEN ab.month = em.min_month THEN ab.avg_balance END) AS avg_balance_difference
FROM extreme_months em
JOIN avg_balance_per_extreme_month ab
  ON ab.month = em.max_month OR ab.month = em.min_month
;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Get each legislator's first term start date and filter for the cohort
cohort AS (
  SELECT
    l.id AS legislator_id,
    MIN(lt.start_date) AS first_term_start
  FROM legislators l
  JOIN legislators_terms lt ON l.id = lt.legislator_id
  WHERE DATE(lt.start_date) BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'
  GROUP BY l.id
),

-- For each legislator in cohort, get max office end date across all terms
cohort_with_end AS (
  SELECT
    c.legislator_id,
    c.first_term_start,
    MAX(lt.end_date) AS last_term_end
  FROM cohort c
  JOIN legislators_terms lt ON c.legislator_id = lt.legislator_id
  GROUP BY c.legislator_id, c.first_term_start
),

-- Build all 20 retention 'years' (0 to 19) for each legislator
all_years AS (
  SELECT
    cwe.legislator_id,
    cwe.first_term_start,
    cwe.last_term_end,
    y.year_idx,
    DATE(cwe.first_term_start, printf('+%d years','0')) AS year0,
    DATE(cwe.first_term_start, printf('+%d years', y.year_idx)) AS cohort_year_date
  FROM cohort_with_end cwe
  JOIN (SELECT 0 as year_idx UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL
              SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL
              SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL
              SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19) y
),

-- Determine, for each legislator and year, if in office on Dec 31 of that year
retention_flags AS (
  SELECT
    ay.year_idx,
    ay.cohort_year_date,
    ay.legislator_id,
    ay.first_term_start,
    ay.last_term_end,
    -- Find the Dec 31 date for the Nth cohort year
    DATE(STRFTIME('%Y', ay.cohort_year_date) || '-12-31') AS year_end_date,
    -- Retained if last_term_end is null or after this year_end_date
    CASE
      WHEN (ay.last_term_end IS NULL OR DATE(ay.last_term_end) >= DATE(STRFTIME('%Y', ay.cohort_year_date) || '-12-31'))
           AND DATE(ay.first_term_start) <= DATE(STRFTIME('%Y', ay.cohort_year_date) || '-12-31')
      THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS retained
  FROM all_years ay
),

-- Compute denominators (cohort size)
cohort_size AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT legislator_id) AS n_cohort FROM cohort
)

SELECT
  rf.year_idx + 1 AS year_number,
  rf.year_end_date,
  ROUND(1.0 * SUM(rf.retained) / cs.n_cohort, 4) AS retention_rate
FROM retention_flags rf
CROSS JOIN cohort_size cs
GROUP BY rf.year_idx, rf.year_end_date
ORDER BY rf.year_idx
LIMIT 20;
```

```sql
WITH base_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.pizza_id,
        o.customer_id,
        n.pizza_name,
        o.exclusions,
        o.extras,
        o.order_time,
        CASE 
            WHEN n.pizza_name = 'Meatlovers' THEN 1
            ELSE 2
        END AS assigned_pizza_id
    FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_names n ON o.pizza_id = n.pizza_id
),
recipe_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        r.pizza_id,
        t.topping_id,
        t.topping_name
    FROM pizza_recipes r
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON ',' || r.toppings || ',' LIKE '%,' || t.topping_id || ',%'
),
order_exclusions AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        t.topping_id
    FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON ',' || ifnull(o.exclusions, '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || t.topping_id || ',%'
),
order_extras AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        t.topping_id
    FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON ',' || ifnull(o.extras, '') || ',' LIKE '%,' || t.topping_id || ',%'
),
order_ingredients AS (
    SELECT 
        bo.order_id,
        bo.customer_id,
        bo.pizza_name,
        bo.order_time,
        rt.topping_name,
        1 as source
    FROM base_orders bo
    LEFT JOIN recipe_toppings rt ON (bo.assigned_pizza_id = rt.pizza_id)
    WHERE rt.topping_name IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        bo.order_id,
        bo.customer_id,
        bo.pizza_name,
        bo.order_time,
        t.topping_name,
        -1 as source
    FROM base_orders bo
    JOIN order_exclusions oe ON bo.order_id = oe.order_id
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON oe.topping_id = t.topping_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        bo.order_id,
        bo.customer_id,
        bo.pizza_name,
        bo.order_time,
        t.topping_name,
        2 as source
    FROM base_orders bo
    JOIN order_extras oe ON bo.order_id = oe.order_id
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON oe.topping_id = t.topping_id
),
agg_ingredients AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        pizza_name,
        order_time,
        topping_name,
        SUM(source) as net_count
    FROM order_ingredients
    GROUP BY order_id, customer_id, pizza_name, order_time, topping_name
    HAVING SUM(source) > 0
),
exploded AS (
    SELECT 
        ai.order_id,
        ai.customer_id,
        ai.pizza_name,
        ai.order_time,
        CASE WHEN ai.net_count > 1 THEN '2x' || ai.topping_name ELSE ai.topping_name END as ingr,
        ai.net_count
    FROM agg_ingredients ai
),
sorted_ingredients AS (
    SELECT 
        e.order_id,
        e.customer_id,
        e.pizza_name,
        e.order_time,
        GROUP_CONCAT(e.ingr, ', ') as ingredient_set
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            *,
            CASE WHEN net_count > 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END as sort_group
        FROM exploded
        ORDER BY order_id, sort_group, ingr
    ) e
    GROUP BY e.order_id, e.customer_id, e.pizza_name, e.order_time
)
SELECT 
    si.order_id, 
    si.customer_id,
    si.pizza_name,
    (si.pizza_name || ': ' || ifnull(si.ingredient_set, '')) AS final_ingredients
FROM sorted_ingredients si
ORDER BY si.order_id ASC;
```

```sql
    SELECT
        region,
        platform,
        age_band,
        demographic,
        customer_type,
        CASE 
            WHEN week_date BETWEEN (SELECT pre_start FROM boundary_dates) AND (SELECT pre_end FROM boundary_dates) THEN 'pre'
            WHEN week_date BETWEEN (SELECT post_start FROM boundary_dates) AND (SELECT post_end FROM boundary_dates) THEN 'post'
        END AS period,
        SUM(sales) AS total_sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales, boundary_dates
    WHERE week_date BETWEEN (SELECT pre_start FROM boundary_dates) AND (SELECT post_end FROM boundary_dates)
    GROUP BY region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type, period
),
sales_pct_change_by_attrvalue AS (
    SELECT

        platform,
        age_band,

        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN period = 'post' THEN total_sales END),0) AS post_sales,
```
```sql
        CASE
```

# Introduction to the RFM Model

The RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) model segments and scores customers based on three key dimensions:

• Recency (R): How long it has been since the customer’s last purchase. A lower R score (e.g., R = 1) indicates a very recent purchase, while a higher R score (e.g., R = 5) indicates a longer time since the last purchase.

• Frequency (F): How often the customer purchases within a given time period. A lower F score (e.g., F = 1) signifies that the customer buys very frequently, whereas a higher F score (e.g., F = 5) indicates less frequent purchasing.

• Monetary (M): The total amount of money the customer spends. A lower M score (e.g., M = 1) indicates higher overall spending, while a higher M score (e.g., M = 5) signifies lower spending over the measured period.

Each customer’s R, F, and M scores are determined by their respective percentiles when compared to other customers. By concatenating the three scores, you get an “RFM cell”—for instance, a customer with R=1, F=5, and M=2 would fall into the 152 segment.

# RFM Segmentation Calculation

After scoring customers on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary values, the next step is to group them into segments that require different marketing or sales strategies. Typically:

1. Determine each customer’s recency score (R) from 1 to 5 (1 = very recent purchase, 5 = not recent).  
2. Determine each customer’s frequency score (F) from 1 to 5 (1 = most frequent purchases, 5 = least frequent).  
3. Determine each customer’s monetary score (M) from 1 to 5 (1 = highest spending, 5 = lowest spending).  
4. Concatenate these three scores into an RFM score (e.g., 153, 514).

By analyzing the distribution of RFM scores and placing them into buckets—for example, “Champions,” “Loyal Customers,” “At Risk,” “Lost,” etc.—you can tailor marketing, sales, and retention strategies to maximize the potential of each segment. 

For instance, a “Champion” (R=1, F=1, M=1) is a recent, frequent, and high-spending user who is highly valuable to your business, whereas a “Lost” customer (e.g., R=5, F=5, M=5) may require re-engagement offers or might no longer be cost-effective to target. Different segments can thus be prioritized based on their profitability and likelihood of responding positively to marketing efforts.

## RFM Segmentation Logic

Customers are assigned to specific segments (RFM Buckets) based on a combination of their Recency, Frequency, and Monetary scores. The segmentation logic is as follows:

- **Champions**: Customers who have made a recent purchase, with high frequency and high monetary value. These are considered the most valuable customers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Can't Lose Them**: Previously frequent and high-spending customers who have not made a recent purchase. These customers are at risk of leaving and need attention.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 2.

- **Hibernating**: Customers whose last purchase was a while ago, with low to moderate frequency and spending. These customers might have lost interest in the products.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 3 and 6.

- **Lost**: Customers who have not purchased in a long time and have low frequency and monetary value. These customers are likely lost.
  - Criteria: Recency = 4 or 5 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

- **Loyal Customers**: Customers who are frequent buyers with decent spending levels, and they have made a purchase relatively recently. These customers are likely to be very loyal.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 or 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 1 and 4.

- **Needs Attention**: Customers whose purchase frequency and spending are moderate. They haven't bought very recently, but they could be incentivized to become more active.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.

- **Recent Users**: Customers who made a purchase recently, but their frequency and spending are moderate. These are relatively new or inconsistent buyers.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 8.

- **Potential Loyalists**: Customers who show potential to become loyal customers. They have good frequency and monetary scores, and they have made recent purchases. With the right engagement, they could become loyal customers.
  - Criteria:
    - Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 6.
    - OR Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 5 and 8.

- **Price Sensitive**: Customers who have made recent purchases but tend to spend less, indicating they may be more sensitive to price.
  - Criteria: Recency = 1 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **Promising**: These customers exhibit high potential with decent frequency and monetary scores, and they could become more valuable over time.
  - Criteria: Recency = 2 and Frequency + Monetary score between 9 and 10.

- **About to Sleep**: Customers whose frequency and spending are low, and their last purchase was some time ago. These customers are likely to become inactive.
  - Criteria: Recency = 3 and Frequency + Monetary score between 7 and 10.

## Summary

This segmentation logic groups customers based on their behavior in terms of when they last purchased (Recency), how often they purchase (Frequency), and how much they spend (Monetary). By understanding which group a customer belongs to, organizations can tailor marketing strategies to engage the right audience more effectively, improving customer retention and maximizing value.

```sql
WITH seller_sales AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold,
        SUM(oi.price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales,
        AVG(oi.price) AS avg_item_price
    FROM order_items oi
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),
seller_reviews AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        AVG(CAST(orv.review_score AS FLOAT)) AS avg_review_score
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN order_reviews orv ON oi.order_id = orv.order_id
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),
seller_packing_times AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        AVG(julianday(o.shipping_limit_date) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) AS avg_packing_time_days
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
),
category_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.product_category_name,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_category_quantity
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY p.product_category_name
),
top_categories AS (
    SELECT
        cst.product_category_name,
        pct.product_category_name_english,
        cst.total_category_quantity,
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cst.total_category_quantity DESC) AS category_rank
    FROM category_sales cst
    JOIN product_category_name_translation pct ON cst.product_category_name = pct.product_category_name
)
SELECT
    s.seller_id,
    se.seller_city,
    se.seller_state,
    ss.total_products_sold,
    ss.total_sales,
    ss.avg_item_price,
    sr.avg_review_score,
    spt.avg_packing_time_days,
    tc.product_category_name_english AS top_category_english,
    tc.total_category_quantity AS top_category_sales_volume
FROM sellers se
JOIN seller_sales ss ON se.seller_id = ss.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_reviews sr ON se.seller_id = sr.seller_id
LEFT JOIN seller_packing_times spt ON se.seller_id = spt.seller_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        pct.product_category_name_english,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_category_quantity,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY oi.seller_id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS rn
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN product_category_name_translation pct ON p.product_category_name = pct.product_category_name
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id, p.product_category_name
) tc ON se.seller_id = tc.seller_id AND tc.rn = 1
WHERE ss.total_products_sold > 100
ORDER BY ss.total_sales DESC;
```

```sql
WITH sales_data AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS year_month,
    SUM(amount) AS monthly_sales,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY strftime('%Y-%m', order_date)) AS month_num
  FROM orderlines
  JOIN orders ON orderlines.order_id = orders.order_id
  WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
    AND order_date >= '2016-01-01'
    AND order_date < '2019-01-01'
  GROUP BY product_id, year_month
),
-- Step 1: Calculate Centered Moving Average (CMA) for each month (window: 5 before + 6 after and 6 before + 5 after)
cma_calc AS (
  SELECT
    sd1.product_id,
    sd1.year_month,
    sd1.month_num,
    sd1.monthly_sales,
    (
      -- Average of two overlapping 12-month windows centered at current month
      (
        COALESCE((SELECT AVG(monthly_sales)
                  FROM sales_data sd2
                  WHERE sd2.product_id = sd1.product_id AND sd2.month_num BETWEEN (sd1.month_num-5) AND (sd1.month_num+6)), 0)
      +
        COALESCE((SELECT AVG(monthly_sales)
                  FROM sales_data sd3
                  WHERE sd3.product_id = sd1.product_id AND sd3.month_num BETWEEN (sd1.month_num-6) AND (sd1.month_num+5)), 0)
      )/2.0 AS cma
    FROM sales_data sd1
),
-- Step 2: Restrict to months 7 - 30 for seasonality/ratio modeling
seasonality_range AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    (monthly_sales / NULLIF(cma,0)) AS sales_to_cma_ratio
  FROM cma_calc
  WHERE month_num BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),
-- Step 3: Estimate seasonality multiplicative index for each of 12 calendar months (using average sales-to-CMA ratio)
seasonality_index AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    CAST(substr(year_month,6,2) AS INTEGER) as month_num_in_year,
    AVG(sales_to_cma_ratio) AS seasonality_factor
  FROM seasonality_range
  GROUP BY product_id, month_num_in_year
),
-- Step 4: Prepare regressor input (dependent: monthly_sales / seasonality_factor, independent: time index)
deseasonalized AS (
  SELECT
    sr.product_id,
    sr.month_num,
    sr.monthly_sales / NULLIF(si.seasonality_factor,0) AS deseasonalized_sales
  FROM seasonality_range sr
  JOIN seasonality_index si
    ON sr.product_id = si.product_id
   AND CAST(substr(sr.year_month,6,2) AS INTEGER) = si.month_num_in_year
),
-- Step 5: Regression coefficients (weighted regression: weight is seasonality factor)
regression_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.product_id,
    COUNT(*) as N,
    SUM(month_num) as Sx,
    SUM(deseasonalized_sales) as Sy,
    SUM(month_num * deseasonalized_sales) as Sxy,
    SUM(month_num * month_num) as Sxx
  FROM deseasonalized d
  GROUP BY d.product_id
),
regression_coeffs AS (
  SELECT
    r.product_id,
    -- Intercept (a): (Sy*Sxx - Sx*Sxy) / (N*Sxx - Sx*Sx)
    (r.Sy * r.Sxx - r.Sx * r.Sxy) * 1.0 / NULLIF((r.N * r.Sxx - r.Sx * r.Sx),0) AS intercept,
    -- Slope (b): (N*Sxy - Sx*Sy) / (N*Sxx - Sx*Sx)
    (r.N * r.Sxy - r.Sx * r.Sy) * 1.0 / NULLIF((r.N * r.Sxx - r.Sx * r.Sx),0) AS slope
  FROM regression_stats r
),
-- Step 6: Forecast for 2018 (months 25~36, i.e. Jan~Dec 2018 since starting from Jan 2016), add back seasonality
forecast_months AS (
  SELECT product_id, (m + 24) AS month_num_2018, m AS forecast_month
  FROM (SELECT 1 m UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6
        UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12)
),
-- join monthly seasonality index for each forecast month
forecast_with_seasonality AS (
  SELECT
    fm.product_id,
    fm.forecast_month,
    rc.intercept + rc.slope * fm.month_num_2018 AS forecast_deseasonalized,
    si.seasonality_factor,
    (rc.intercept + rc.slope * fm.month_num_2018) * si.seasonality_factor AS forecasted_sales
  FROM forecast_months fm
  JOIN regression_coeffs rc ON rc.product_id = fm.product_id
  JOIN seasonality_index si
    ON si.product_id = fm.product_id
   AND si.month_num_in_year = fm.forecast_month
)
-- Step 7: Compute average forecasted annual sales for 2018 for each product
SELECT
  product_id,
  AVG(forecasted_sales) AS avg_forecasted_annual_sales_2018
FROM forecast_with_seasonality
GROUP BY product_id
```

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

```sql
    SELECT 
        CASE WHEN a1.city < a2.city THEN a1.city ELSE a2.city END AS city1,
        CASE WHEN a1.city < a2.city THEN a2.city ELSE a1.city END AS city2,
        a1.airport_code AS airport1, a2.airport_code AS airport2,
        a1.latitude_deg AS lat1, a1.longitude_deg AS lon1,
        a2.latitude_deg AS lat2, a2.longitude_deg AS lon2
    FROM routes r

    JOIN airports_data a2 ON r.airport2 = a2.airport_code
),
city_pairs AS (
    SELECT city1, city2, lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2
    FROM unique_routes
    GROUP BY city1, city2
),
distances AS (

            )
        ) AS distance_km
    FROM city_pairs
    WHERE city1 = 'Abakan' OR city2 = 'Abakan'
)
```

# Flight Route Distance Calculation

## Introduction

This document describes the method used to calculate the distance between two cities for flight routes. The calculation is based on the Haversine formula, which is commonly used to find the shortest distance between two points on a sphere given their latitude and longitude. This method is especially useful for determining flight distances between airports located in different cities around the world.

## City and Coordinate Extraction

For each flight, the following data is obtained:

- **Departure city** (referred to as `from_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).
- **Arrival city** (referred to as `to_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).

The coordinates are extracted as decimal values, with longitude and latitude represented in degrees. This ensures that trigonometric operations can be applied during the distance calculation.

## Haversine Formula

The Haversine formula is used to calculate the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere using their latitude and longitude. The formula is given as:

\[
d = 2r \cdot \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) + \cos(\phi_1) \cdot \cos(\phi_2) \cdot \sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \lambda}{2}\right)}\right)
\]

Where:

- \( d \) is the distance between the two points (in kilometers).
- \( r \) is the radius of the Earth (approximately 6371 km).
- \( \phi_1 \) and \( \phi_2 \) are the latitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \phi = \phi_2 - \phi_1 \) is the difference in latitudes.
- \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) are the longitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \lambda = \lambda_2 - \lambda_1 \) is the difference in longitudes.

### Conversion to Radians

Since the input coordinates are in degrees, they must be converted to radians before applying the Haversine formula. This conversion is done using the formula:

\[
\text{radians} = \text{degrees} \times \frac{\pi}{180}
\]

## Symmetry of Routes

To identify unique flight routes between two cities, we standardize the order of cities in each route. Specifically, we ensure that the lexicographically smaller city name is always listed as the first city (`city1`), and the larger city is listed as the second city (`city2`). This ensures that a flight from City A to City B is treated the same as a flight from City B to City A.

## Average Route Distance

Once the distances for all flights between two cities are computed, the average distance for each city pair is calculated by summing the distances and dividing by the total number of flights between those cities:

\[
\text{Average Distance} = \frac{\sum \text{Flight Distances}}{\text{Number of Flights}}
\]

## Conclusion

This method of flight route distance calculation provides a reliable way to determine the great-circle distance between cities based on the coordinates of their respective airports. The use of the Haversine formula ensures accurate results for distances on the Earth's surface, making it ideal for aviation and travel analysis.

```sql
        CASE WHEN a1.city < a2.city THEN a1.city ELSE a2.city END AS city1,
        CASE WHEN a1.city < a2.city THEN a2.city ELSE a1.city END AS city2,
        a1.airport_code AS airport1, a2.airport_code AS airport2,
        a1.latitude_deg AS lat1, a1.longitude_deg AS lon1,
        a2.latitude_deg AS lat2, a2.longitude_deg AS lon2
    FROM routes r
    JOIN airports_data a1 ON r.airport1 = a1.airport_code
    JOIN airports_data a2 ON r.airport2 = a2.airport_code
),
city_pairs AS (
    SELECT city1, city2, lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2
    FROM unique_routes
    GROUP BY city1, city2
),
distances AS (
    SELECT
        city1, city2,
        2 * 6371 * 
        ASIN(
            SQRT(
                POWER(SIN(RADIANS((lat2 - lat1) / 2)), 2) +
                COS(RADIANS(lat1)) * COS(RADIANS(lat2)) *
                POWER(SIN(RADIANS((lon2 - lon1) / 2)), 2)
            )
        ) AS distance_km
    FROM city_pairs
    WHERE city1 = 'Abakan' OR city2 = 'Abakan'
)
SELECT MAX(distance_km) AS longest_route_km
FROM distances;
```

```sql
    FROM Track
```

```sql
WITH us_products AS (
  SELECT s.product_id, s.city, s.calendar_quarter_id, s.sales_amount
  FROM sales s
  JOIN countries c ON s.country_id = c.country_id
  WHERE c.country_name = 'United States' AND s.promo_id = 999
    AND s.calendar_quarter_id IN (1772, 1776)
),
sales_by_city_quarter AS (
  SELECT city, calendar_quarter_id, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales
  FROM us_products
  GROUP BY city, calendar_quarter_id
),
city_growth AS (
  SELECT
    q19.city,
    q19.total_sales AS sales_2019,
    q20.total_sales AS sales_2020,
    (CAST(q20.total_sales AS FLOAT) - q19.total_sales) / q19.total_sales AS growth_rate
  FROM
    (SELECT * FROM sales_by_city_quarter WHERE calendar_quarter_id = 1772) q19
    JOIN (SELECT * FROM sales_by_city_quarter WHERE calendar_quarter_id = 1776) q20
      ON q19.city = q20.city
  WHERE q19.total_sales > 0
),
qualifying_cities AS (
  SELECT city
  FROM city_growth
  WHERE growth_rate >= 0.2
),
filtered_sales AS (
  SELECT s.product_id, s.calendar_quarter_id, s.sales_amount
  FROM us_products s
  WHERE s.city IN (SELECT city FROM qualifying_cities)
),
product_total_sales AS (
  SELECT product_id, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales
  FROM filtered_sales
  GROUP BY product_id
),
top_20pct_threshold AS (
  SELECT
    PERCENTILE_DISC(0.8) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_sales) AS threshold
  FROM product_total_sales
),
top_products AS (
  SELECT product_id, total_sales
  FROM product_total_sales, top_20pct_threshold
  WHERE total_sales >= threshold
),
product_sales_share AS (
  SELECT
    f.product_id,
    f.calendar_quarter_id,
    SUM(f.sales_amount) AS product_sales,
    ts.total_sales AS total_quarter_sales
  FROM filtered_sales f
  JOIN (
    SELECT calendar_quarter_id, SUM(sales_amount) AS total_sales
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY calendar_quarter_id
  ) ts
    ON f.calendar_quarter_id = ts.calendar_quarter_id
  WHERE f.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM top_products)
  GROUP BY f.product_id, f.calendar_quarter_id
),
product_sales_share_change AS (
  SELECT
    p.product_id,
    (p2020.product_sales * 1.0 / p2020.total_quarter_sales) - (p2019.product_sales * 1.0 / p2019.total_quarter_sales) AS pct_point_change
  FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM top_products) p
    JOIN product_sales_share p2019 ON p.product_id = p2019.product_id AND p2019.calendar_quarter_id = 1772
    JOIN product_sales_share p2020 ON p.product_id = p2020.product_id AND p2020.calendar_quarter_id = 1776
)
SELECT p.product_id
FROM product_sales_share_change p
ORDER BY ABS(p.pct_point_change) ASC
LIMIT 1;
```

# Special Words Definition

## Batting Average
- Batting average is a measure of a batsman's performance, calculated by dividing the total number of runs scored by the number of times they have been dismissed. A higher batting average indicates a more consistent and successful batsman.
- Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Dismissals

## Strike Rate
- In batting, strike rate indicates the scoring rate of a batsman, showing the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. A higher strike rate reflects an aggressive and fast-scoring batsman.
- Strike Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

## Wickets Taken
- Wickets taken refers to the total number of times a bowler has successfully dismissed an opposing batsman. This statistic is a core measure of a bowler's effectiveness and impact on the game.

## Economy Rate
- Economy rate measures a bowler's efficiency by indicating the average number of runs conceded per over (6 balls) bowled. A lower economy rate shows greater control and efficiency in restricting the opposition's scoring.
- Economy Rate = (Total Runs Conceded ÷ Balls Bowled) × 6

## Wickets Taken
- The number of times a bowler successfully dismisses a batsman in a single match.  This metric is a direct indicator of the bowler's effectiveness, showing how many players they were able to remove from play.

## Runs Given
- The total number of runs scored by the batting side off a particular bowler’s deliveries in a single match.  This value reflects the runs the bowler has conceded to the batting team, and a lower runs-given value is typically favorable for the bowler's performance.

# Overtake Label Classification

In racing, overtakes are categorized into different states based on specific conditions, reflecting the circumstances in which the overtaking occurred. Below are the classifications and their detailed explanations:

## 1. R (Retirement) - Overtake during Retirement
An overtake is labeled as **R (Retirement)** if the overtaken driver retired on the same lap as the overtake. This indicates that the overtake occurred just before or during the overtaken driver's retirement, meaning they could no longer continue the race after that lap.

## 2. P (Pit) - Overtake related to Pit Stops
An overtake is classified as **P (Pit)** under two scenarios:
   - **Pit Entry**: If the overtake occurred while the overtaken driver was entering the pit lane, and the driver pitted on the same lap, it indicates that the overtaking happened due to the overtaken driver reducing speed to enter the pit lane.
   - **Pit Exit**: If the overtake occurred as the overtaken driver was exiting the pit lane, especially if the driver pitted on the previous lap and the time gap between the drivers was less than a typical pit stop duration. This suggests that the overtake happened while the overtaken driver was potentially at a lower speed, rejoining the race track from the pit lane.

## 3. S (Start) - Overtake at Race Start
If the overtake took place on the first lap of the race, and the two drivers were within two grid positions of each other at the start, the overtake is classified as **S (Start)**. This classification indicates that the overtake was part of the initial racing shuffle during the race's launch phase, where close position changes are common.

## 4. T (Track) - Overtake under Normal Racing Conditions
If none of the above conditions apply, the overtake is categorized as **T (Track)**, meaning it occurred during normal racing conditions on the track, without any external factors like pit stops or retirements influencing the outcome. This is the default classification for overtakes that happen during regular competition.

---

These classifications help to identify and record the context of each overtake with clarity, ensuring accurate representation of race dynamics.

```sql
WITH finished_orders_per_month AS (

FROM pivoted

WHERE
  feb_orders IS NOT NULL
  AND mar_orders IS NOT NULL
  AND (CAST(mar_orders AS FLOAT) - feb_orders) / feb_orders > 0.2
```

```sql
    FROM university_faculty
    GROUP BY rank
```

```sql
WITH Match_Wins AS (
    SELECT
        m.league_id,
        m.home_team_api_id AS team_id,
        CASE WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS win
    FROM Match m
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        m.league_id,
        m.away_team_api_id AS team_id,
        CASE WHEN m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS win
    FROM Match m
),
Team_League AS (
    -- All teams paired with all leagues they ever participated in a match
    SELECT DISTINCT m.league_id, m.home_team_api_id AS team_id
    FROM Match m
    UNION
    SELECT DISTINCT m.league_id, m.away_team_api_id AS team_id
    FROM Match m
),
Team_Wins AS (
    SELECT
        tl.league_id,
        tl.team_id,
        COALESCE(SUM(mw.win), 0) AS total_wins
    FROM Team_League tl
    LEFT JOIN Match_Wins mw
        ON tl.league_id = mw.league_id AND tl.team_id = mw.team_id
    GROUP BY tl.league_id, tl.team_id
),
Min_Wins_Per_League AS (
    SELECT
        league_id,
        MIN(total_wins) AS min_wins
    FROM Team_Wins
    GROUP BY league_id
)
SELECT
    l.name AS league_name,
    t.team_long_name AS team_name,
    tw.total_wins
FROM Min_Wins_Per_League mwpl
JOIN Team_Wins tw
    ON mwpl.league_id = tw.league_id

JOIN League l
    ON l.id = tw.league_id
JOIN Team t
    ON t.team_api_id = tw.team_id
-- pick only a single team per league in case of ties
WHERE tw.team_id IN (
    SELECT tw2.team_id
    FROM Team_Wins tw2
    WHERE tw2.league_id = tw.league_id
    ORDER BY tw2.team_id
    LIMIT 1
)
ORDER BY l.name;
```

```sql
LEFT JOIN first_action f

WHERE
    (a.search_type IS NOT NULL AND a.search_type != '')
```

```sql
WITH EnglishCourses AS (
  SELECT s.StudentID, s.LastName, scs.Grade
  FROM Students s
  JOIN Student_Class_Status scs ON s.StudentID = scs.StudentID
  JOIN Classes c ON scs.ClassID = c.ClassID
  JOIN Subjects subj ON c.SubjectID = subj.SubjectID
  WHERE scs.ClassStatus = 2
    AND subj.SubjectName = 'English'
),
Ranked AS (
  SELECT
    StudentID,
    LastName,
    Grade,
    (
      SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Grade) 
      FROM EnglishCourses ec2 
      WHERE ec2.Grade >= ec1.Grade
    ) AS RankDesc
  FROM EnglishCourses ec1
),
StudentCount AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students FROM EnglishCourses
),
WithQuintile AS (
  SELECT 
    r.LastName,
    r.Grade,
    r.RankDesc,
    sc.total_students,
    CASE
      WHEN CAST(r.RankDesc AS FLOAT) / sc.total_students <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
      WHEN CAST(r.RankDesc AS FLOAT) / sc.total_students <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
      WHEN CAST(r.RankDesc AS FLOAT) / sc.total_students <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
      WHEN CAST(r.RankDesc AS FLOAT) / sc.total_students <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
      ELSE 'Fifth'
    END AS Quintile
  FROM Ranked r
  CROSS JOIN StudentCount sc
)
SELECT LastName, Quintile
FROM WithQuintile
ORDER BY
  CASE Quintile
    WHEN 'First' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Second' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Third' THEN 3
    WHEN 'Fourth' THEN 4
    WHEN 'Fifth' THEN 5
    ELSE 6
  END,
  LastName
;
```

```sql
    FROM fr_sales

        END AS proj_2021
    FROM monthly_combined
```

```sql
WITH male_la_legislators AS (
    SELECT l.id, l.first_name, l.last_name, l.gender, t.state, MIN(t.start_date) AS first_term_start
    FROM legislators l
    JOIN legislators_terms t ON l.id = t.legislator_id
    WHERE l.gender = 'M' AND t.state = 'LA'
    GROUP BY l.id
),
years_elapsed AS (
    SELECT
        mll.id,
        mll.first_term_start,
        CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) AS start_year,
        y.year,
        y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) AS years_since_first_term
    FROM male_la_legislators mll
    JOIN (
        -- every possible year to check
        SELECT DISTINCT CAST(strftime('%Y', date) AS INTEGER) AS year
        FROM legislation_date_dim
    ) y
    ON y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) > 30
    AND y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) < 50
),
active_terms AS (
    SELECT
        ye.id,
        ye.year,
        ye.years_since_first_term
    FROM years_elapsed ye
    JOIN legislators_terms t
      ON ye.id = t.legislator_id
     AND DATE(t.start_date) <= DATE(ye.year || '-12-31')
     AND (t.end_date IS NULL OR DATE(t.end_date) >= DATE(ye.year || '-12-31'))
)
SELECT
    years_since_first_term AS years_elapsed,
    COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS active_legislator_count
FROM active_terms
GROUP BY years_since_first_term
ORDER BY years_since_first_term;
```

```sql
    SELECT l.id, l.first_name, l.last_name, l.gender, t.state, MIN(t.start_date) AS first_term_start
    FROM legislators l
    JOIN legislators_terms t ON l.id = t.legislator_id
    WHERE l.gender = 'M' AND t.state = 'LA'
    GROUP BY l.id
),
years_elapsed AS (
    SELECT
        mll.id,
        mll.first_term_start,
        CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) AS start_year,
        y.year,
        y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) AS years_since_first_term
    FROM male_la_legislators mll
    JOIN (
        -- every possible year to check
        SELECT DISTINCT CAST(strftime('%Y', date) AS INTEGER) AS year
        FROM legislation_date_dim
    ) y
    ON y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) > 30
    AND y.year - CAST(strftime('%Y', mll.first_term_start) AS INTEGER) < 50
),
active_terms AS (
    SELECT
        ye.id,
        ye.year,
        ye.years_since_first_term
    FROM years_elapsed ye
    JOIN legislators_terms t
      ON ye.id = t.legislator_id
     AND DATE(t.start_date) <= DATE(ye.year || '-12-31')
     AND (t.end_date IS NULL OR DATE(t.end_date) >= DATE(ye.year || '-12-31'))
)
SELECT
    years_since_first_term AS years_elapsed,
    COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS active_legislator_count
FROM active_terms
GROUP BY years_since_first_term
ORDER BY years_since_first_term;
```

```sql
WITH overtakes AS (
  SELECT
    lp.race_id,
    lp.lap,
    lp.position,
    lp.driver_id,
    LAG(lp.position) OVER (PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap) AS prev_position,
    LAG(lp.lap) OVER (PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap) AS prev_lap
  FROM lap_positions lp
),
position_changes AS (
  -- Only consider laps beyond the first lap (exclude start movements)
  -- Exclude pit-in/out laps by joining with pit_stops table
  SELECT
    o.race_id,
    o.lap,
    o.driver_id,
    o.prev_position,
    o.position,
    o.prev_lap
  FROM overtakes o
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON o.race_id = ps.race_id AND o.driver_id = ps.driver_id AND (o.lap = ps.lap or o.prev_lap = ps.lap)
  WHERE
    o.prev_lap IS NOT NULL
    AND o.lap > 1
    AND o.prev_position != o.position
    AND ps.driver_id IS NULL -- Exclude pit-in/out laps
),
all_drivers_in_lap AS (
  -- For each lap, find all driver positions before and after
  SELECT
    lp.race_id,
    lp.lap,
    lp.driver_id,
    lp.position
  FROM lap_positions lp
  WHERE lp.lap > 1
),
position_gains AS (
  -- Who overtook whom (i.e., a driver moving ahead of another)
  SELECT
    pc.race_id,
    pc.lap,
    pc.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
    pc.prev_position,
    pc.position,
    adil.driver_id AS overtaken_id
  FROM position_changes pc
  JOIN all_drivers_in_lap adil
    ON pc.race_id = adil.race_id
    AND pc.lap = adil.lap
    AND adil.driver_id != pc.driver_id
    AND pc.prev_position > adil.position -- Was behind previously
    AND pc.position <= adil.position -- Is now ahead or on same spot
),
overtake_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d1.driver_id,
    d1.forename || ' ' || d1.surname AS full_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT (pg.race_id || '_' || pg.lap || '_' || pg.overtaken_id)) AS overtakes_made
  FROM drivers d1
  LEFT JOIN position_gains pg
    ON d1.driver_id = pg.overtaker_id
  GROUP BY d1.driver_id
),
being_overtaken_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d1.driver_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT (pg.race_id || '_' || pg.lap || '_' || pg.overtaker_id)) AS overtakes_suffered
  FROM drivers d1
  LEFT JOIN position_gains pg
    ON d1.driver_id = pg.overtaken_id
  GROUP BY d1.driver_id
)
SELECT
  ods.full_name
FROM overtake_stats ods
JOIN being_overtaken_stats bos
  ON ods.driver_id = bos.driver_id
WHERE bos.overtakes_suffered > ods.overtakes_made
ORDER BY ods.full_name;
```

```sql
WITH italian_customers AS (
  SELECT c.cust_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
),
dec_sales AS (
  SELECT s.cust_id, s.prod_id, s.quantity_sold, t.calendar_month_number, t.calendar_year
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE t.calendar_month_number = 12 AND t.calendar_year = 2021
),
profit_per_customer AS (
  SELECT ic.cust_id, SUM(ds.quantity_sold * (p.prod_list_price - p.prod_min_price)) AS total_profit
  FROM italian_customers ic
  JOIN dec_sales ds ON ic.cust_id = ds.cust_id
  JOIN products p ON ds.prod_id = p.prod_id
  GROUP BY ic.cust_id
),
profit_range AS (
  SELECT MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit, MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit FROM profit_per_customer
),
profits_with_bucket AS (
  SELECT
    ppc.total_profit,
    ppc.cust_id,
    pr.min_profit,
    pr.max_profit,
    (CASE WHEN pr.max_profit = pr.min_profit THEN 1
          ELSE CAST(1 + (ppc.total_profit - pr.min_profit) * 10.0 / (pr.max_profit - pr.min_profit) AS INTEGER) END) AS bucket
  FROM profit_per_customer ppc, profit_range pr
)
SELECT
  bucket,
  COUNT(cust_id) AS num_customers,
  MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit_in_bucket,
  MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit_in_bucket
FROM profits_with_bucket
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY bucket
```

WITH italian_customers AS (
  SELECT c.cust_id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'Italy'
),
dec_sales AS (
  SELECT s.cust_id, s.prod_id, s.quantity_sold, t.calendar_month_number, t.calendar_year
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE t.calendar_month_number = 12 AND t.calendar_year = 2021
),
profit_per_customer AS (
  SELECT ic.cust_id, SUM(ds.quantity_sold * (p.prod_list_price - p.prod_min_price)) AS total_profit
  FROM italian_customers ic
  JOIN dec_sales ds ON ic.cust_id = ds.cust_id
  JOIN products p ON ds.prod_id = p.prod_id
  GROUP BY ic.cust_id
),
profit_range AS (
  SELECT MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit, MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit FROM profit_per_customer
),
profits_with_bucket AS (
  SELECT
    ppc.total_profit,
    ppc.cust_id,
    pr.min_profit,
    pr.max_profit,
    (CASE WHEN pr.max_profit = pr.min_profit THEN 1
          ELSE CAST(1 + (ppc.total_profit - pr.min_profit) * 10.0 / (pr.max_profit - pr.min_profit) AS INTEGER) END) AS bucket
  FROM profit_per_customer ppc, profit_range pr
)
SELECT
  bucket,
  COUNT(cust_id) AS num_customers,
  MIN(total_profit) AS min_profit_in_bucket,
  MAX(total_profit) AS max_profit_in_bucket
FROM profits_with_bucket
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY bucket;

    FROM sales s
```sql
    JOIN promotions pr ON s.promo_id = pr.promo_id
    JOIN channels c ON s.channel_id = c.channel_id
    WHERE s.cust_id IN (SELECT country_id FROM fr)
      AND pr.promo_total_id = 1

    GROUP BY s.prod_id, sales_year, sales_month
),

    SELECT 
        prod_id, 
        sales_month,
        MAX(CASE WHEN sales_year = '2019' THEN amount_sold ELSE NULL END) AS sales_2019,

    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY prod_id, sales_month
),
projected_2021 AS (
    SELECT 
        prod_id, 
        sales_month,
        ((sales_2020 - sales_2019) * 1.0 / NULLIF(sales_2019, 0)) * sales_2020 + sales_2020 AS proj_2021
    FROM pivoted_sales
    WHERE sales_2019 IS NOT NULL AND sales_2019 != 0 AND sales_2020 IS NOT NULL
),
proj_2021_with_currency AS (
    SELECT

        p.proj_2021,
        cu.to_us

),

        ROUND(AVG(proj_2021 * COALESCE(to_us,1)), 2) AS avg_proj_2021_usd
    FROM proj_2021_with_currency
    GROUP BY sales_month
)

ORDER BY month;
```

Provided benchmark documentation:
## Projection Calculation Method

### Steps for Projection Calculation

1. **Aggregate Historical Sales Data**

   - **Data Collection**: Gather sales data for products sold in France, including sales amounts each month for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021.
   - **Summarize Sales**: Sum up the sales amounts for each product, country, month, and year.

2. **Calculate Average Sales**

   - **Monthly Averages**: Compute the average sales amount for each product and month across all available months to establish a baseline of typical sales.

3. **Project Sales for 2021**

   - **Identify Changes**: Determine how sales changed from 2019 to 2020 for each product and month. Calculate the percentage change in sales from 2019 to 2020.
   - **Apply Changes**: Use this percentage change to estimate the sales for each month in 2021.

   **Projection Formula**:
   - For 2021:
     - Calculate the difference in sales between 2020 and 2019.
     - Compute the percentage change relative to 2019 sales.
     - Apply this percentage change to the 2020 sales to estimate 2021 sales.
     - The formula used in the SQL query is:

       ```plaintext
       (((Sales in 2020 - Sales in 2019) / Sales in 2019) * Sales in 2020) + Sales in 2020
       ```

     - This formula calculates the projected sales for 2021 based on the observed trend from 2019 to 2020.

   - For other years (not 2021):
     - Use the average sales value calculated for each month.

4. **Adjust for Currency Conversion**

   - **Conversion Rates**: Convert the projected sales figures into USD using monthly conversion rates.
   - **Currency Adjustment**: Multiply the projected sales figures by the conversion rates to adjust to USD. If specific rates are not available, use a default rate of 1.

5. **Calculate Monthly Averages in USD**

   - **Monthly Projections**: Compute the average projected sales for each month in 2021, adjusting for currency conversion. Round the results to two decimal places.

6. **Compile Results**

   - **Organize Data**: Arrange the projected sales figures in a report, showing the estimated sales for each month in USD.

### Summary

```sql
WITH parsed_volumes AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    ticker,
    CASE
      WHEN TRIM(volume) = '-' THEN 0
      WHEN TRIM(volume) LIKE '%M' THEN
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(volume), 'M', ''), ',', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000000
      WHEN TRIM(volume) LIKE '%K' THEN
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(volume), 'K', ''), ',', '') AS FLOAT) * 1000
      ELSE
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(volume), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS FLOAT)
    END AS volume_value
  FROM bitcoin_prices
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
),
volumes_with_prev AS (
  SELECT
    pv1.date,
    pv1.ticker,
    pv1.volume_value,
    (
      SELECT pv2.volume_value
      FROM parsed_volumes pv2
      WHERE pv2.ticker = pv1.ticker
        AND pv2.date < pv1.date
        AND pv2.volume_value > 0
      ORDER BY pv2.date DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS prev_non_zero_volume
  FROM parsed_volumes pv1
)
SELECT
  date,
  ticker,
  volume_value AS volume,
  prev_non_zero_volume,
  CASE
    WHEN prev_non_zero_volume IS NOT NULL AND prev_non_zero_volume != 0
      THEN ROUND( (volume_value - prev_non_zero_volume) / prev_non_zero_volume * 100, 4)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pct_change
FROM volumes_with_prev
ORDER BY ticker, date;
```

```sql
WITH non_stack_scores AS (
  SELECT 
    m.name, 
    m.version, 
    ms.step, 
    MAX(ms.test_score) AS max_non_stack_score
  FROM model_score ms
  JOIN model m ON ms.model_id = m.id
  WHERE ms.L1_model IS NOT NULL AND ms.L1_model != 'Stack'
  GROUP BY m.name, m.version, ms.step
),
stack_scores AS (
  SELECT 
    m.name, 
    m.version, 
    ms.step, 
    ms.test_score AS stack_test_score,
    ms.L1_model
  FROM model_score ms
  JOIN model m ON ms.model_id = m.id
  WHERE ms.L1_model = 'Stack'
),
model_status AS (
  SELECT
    s.name,
    s.version,
    s.step,
    s.L1_model,
    CASE 
      WHEN n.max_non_stack_score < s.stack_test_score THEN 'strong'
      WHEN n.max_non_stack_score = s.stack_test_score THEN 'soft'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS status
  FROM stack_scores s
  LEFT JOIN non_stack_scores n
    ON s.name = n.name AND s.version = n.version AND s.step = n.step
  WHERE n.max_non_stack_score IS NOT NULL
),
status_counts AS (
  SELECT
    L1_model,
    status,
    COUNT(*) AS count
  FROM model_status
  WHERE status IN ('strong', 'soft')
  GROUP BY L1_model, status
),
most_frequent AS (
  SELECT
    status,
    L1_model,
    count,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY count DESC) as rnk
  FROM status_counts
)
SELECT
  status,
  L1_model,
  count
FROM most_frequent
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY status, L1_model;
```

```sql
WITH filtered_words AS (
  SELECT
    word,
    LENGTH(word) AS len
  FROM word_list
  WHERE LENGTH(word) BETWEEN 4 AND 5
    AND word LIKE 'r%'
),
word_anagram_keys AS (
  SELECT
    word,
    len,
    -- generate an anagram key by sorting characters (case-sensitive)
    (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(ch, '') FROM (
      SELECT SUBSTR(word, n, 1) AS ch
      FROM (
        WITH RECURSIVE chars(n) AS (
          SELECT 1
          UNION ALL
          SELECT n+1 FROM chars WHERE n < LENGTH(word)
        )
        SELECT n FROM chars
      )
      ORDER BY ch
    )) AS anagram_key
  FROM filtered_words
),
anagram_counts AS (
  SELECT
    w1.word,
    w1.len,
    w1.anagram_key,
    COUNT(DISTINCT w2.word) AS anagram_count
  FROM word_anagram_keys w1
  JOIN word_anagram_keys w2
    ON w1.anagram_key = w2.anagram_key
    AND w1.len = w2.len
    AND w1.word <> w2.word
  GROUP BY w1.word, w1.len, w1.anagram_key
)
SELECT
  word,
  anagram_count
FROM anagram_counts
ORDER BY word
LIMIT 10;
```

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE packaging_hierarchy AS (
  -- Start from all top-level packaging (not inside any other packaging)
  SELECT
    p.id AS top_packaging_id,
    p.name AS top_packaging_name,
    pr.contains_id AS packaging_id,
    pr.qty AS multiplier
  FROM packaging p
  JOIN packaging_relations pr ON p.id = pr.packaging_id
  WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)

  UNION ALL

  -- Traverse deeper into the hierarchy, multiplying quantities
  SELECT
    ph.top_packaging_id,
    ph.top_packaging_name,
    pr.contains_id,
    ph.multiplier * pr.qty
  FROM packaging_hierarchy ph
  JOIN packaging_relations pr ON ph.packaging_id = pr.packaging_id
)
, packaging_to_product AS (
  -- Find products directly contained in lowest-level packaging
  SELECT
    ph.top_packaging_id,
    ph.top_packaging_name,
    inv.product_id,
    ph.multiplier * inv.qty AS total_qty
  FROM packaging_hierarchy ph
  JOIN inventory inv ON ph.packaging_id = inv.id
)
, total_qty_accumulated AS (
  -- Aggregate quantity for each top-level packaging and product
  SELECT
    top_packaging_id,
    top_packaging_name,
    product_id,
    SUM(total_qty) AS accumulated_qty
  FROM packaging_to_product
  GROUP BY top_packaging_id, top_packaging_name, product_id
)
SELECT
  tqa.top_packaging_name AS packaging_name,
  prod.name AS product_name,
  tqa.accumulated_qty
FROM total_qty_accumulated tqa
JOIN products prod ON tqa.product_id = prod.id
WHERE tqa.accumulated_qty > 500
ORDER BY tqa.top_packaging_name, prod.name;
```

```sql
WITH driver_race_appearances AS (
    SELECT
        d.driverId,
        d.forename,
        d.surname,
        r.year,
        r.round,
        results.constructorId,
        r.raceId
    FROM drivers d
    JOIN results ON d.driverId = results.driverId
    JOIN races r ON results.raceId = r.raceId
),
driver_year_races AS (
    SELECT
        driverId,
        year,
        GROUP_CONCAT(round, ',') AS appeared_rounds,
        COUNT(DISTINCT round) AS num_appearances
    FROM driver_race_appearances
    GROUP BY driverId, year
),
all_race_rounds AS (
    SELECT
        r.year,
        GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT r.round, ',') AS all_rounds,
        COUNT(DISTINCT r.round) AS total_rounds
    FROM races r
    GROUP BY r.year
),
driver_missed_ranges AS (
    -- Find missed round ranges per driver per year, only where missed count < 3
    SELECT
        dra.driverId,
        dra.year,
        arr.all_rounds,
        dra.appeared_rounds,
        arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances AS num_missed,
        -- Parse rounds into arrays for later processing (first, last missed)
        arr.all_rounds AS all_rounds_csv,
        dra.appeared_rounds AS appeared_rounds_csv
    FROM driver_year_races dra
    JOIN all_race_rounds arr ON dra.year = arr.year
    WHERE (arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances) > 0 AND (arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances) < 3
),
expanded_missed_rounds AS (
    -- Expand missed rounds for each driver/year
    SELECT
        dmr.driverId,
        dmr.year,
        CAST(value AS INTEGER) AS missed_round
    FROM driver_missed_ranges dmr
    JOIN (
        SELECT
            driverId,
            year,
            all_rounds_csv,
            appeared_rounds_csv,
            -- split rounds into rows: for each round in all_rounds, if not in appeared_rounds, yield it
            substr(all_rounds_csv,
                instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1,
                CASE
                    WHEN instr(substr(all_rounds_csv || ',', instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1), ',') = 0 THEN length(all_rounds_csv)
                    ELSE instr(substr(all_rounds_csv || ',', instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1), ',') - 1
                END
            ) AS value
        FROM driver_missed_ranges
        JOIN (
            SELECT 1 as n UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7
            UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14
            UNION SELECT 15 UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
            -- max races per year is 20 (should be enough)
        )
        WHERE n <= (length(all_rounds_csv) - length(REPLACE(all_rounds_csv, ',', ''))+1)
    ) AS rounds_split
    WHERE value NOT IN (SELECT value FROM (
        SELECT
            substr(appeared_rounds_csv,
                instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1,
                CASE
                    WHEN instr(substr(appeared_rounds_csv || ',', instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1), ',') = 0
                    THEN length(appeared_rounds_csv)
                    ELSE instr(substr(appeared_rounds_csv || ',', instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1), ',') - 1
                END
            ) AS value
        FROM (
            SELECT *
            FROM driver_missed_ranges AS t1
            WHERE t1.driverId = driver_missed_ranges.driverId AND t1.year = driver_missed_ranges.year
        ), (
            SELECT 1 AS n2 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION
            SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14
            UNION SELECT 15 UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
        )
        WHERE n2 <= (length(appeared_rounds_csv) - length(REPLACE(appeared_rounds_csv, ',', ''))+1)
    ))
        AND value != '' AND value IS NOT NULL
),
driver_missed_ranges_final AS (
    -- collapse to one missed range per driver/year
    SELECT
        emr.driverId,
        emr.year,
        MIN(emr.missed_round) AS first_missed_round,
        MAX(emr.missed_round) AS last_missed_round
    FROM expanded_missed_rounds emr
    GROUP BY emr.driverId, emr.year
),
edge_constructor_switch AS (
    -- For each missed range, check constructor before/after missed races
    SELECT
        dmr.driverId,
        dmr.year,
        dmr.first_missed_round,
        dmr.last_missed_round,
        -- Get constructorId right before first missed
        (
            SELECT constructorId
            FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId
              AND dra.year = dmr.year
              AND dra.round = dmr.first_missed_round - 1
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS before_constructorId,
        -- Get constructorId right after last missed
        (
            SELECT constructorId
            FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId
              AND dra.year = dmr.year
              AND dra.round = dmr.last_missed_round + 1
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS after_constructorId
    FROM driver_missed_ranges_final dmr
    WHERE
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId AND dra.year = dmr.year AND dra.round = dmr.first_missed_round - 1
        )
        AND
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId AND dra.year = dmr.year AND dra.round = dmr.last_missed_round + 1
        )
)
SELECT
    AVG(first_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_first_missed_round,
    AVG(last_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_last_missed_round
FROM edge_constructor_switch
WHERE before_constructorId IS NOT NULL AND after_constructorId IS NOT NULL AND before_constructorId != after_constructorId;
```

```sql
WITH driver_race_appearances AS (
    SELECT
        d.driverId,
        d.forename,
        d.surname,
        r.year,
        r.round,
        results.constructorId,
        r.raceId
    FROM drivers d
    JOIN results ON d.driverId = results.driverId
    JOIN races r ON results.raceId = r.raceId
),
driver_year_races AS (
    SELECT
        driverId,
        year,
        GROUP_CONCAT(round, ',') AS appeared_rounds,
        COUNT(DISTINCT round) AS num_appearances
    FROM driver_race_appearances
    GROUP BY driverId, year
),
all_race_rounds AS (
    SELECT
        r.year,
        GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT r.round, ',') AS all_rounds,
        COUNT(DISTINCT r.round) AS total_rounds
    FROM races r
    GROUP BY r.year
),
driver_missed_ranges AS (
    -- Find missed round ranges per driver per year, only where missed count < 3
    SELECT
        dra.driverId,
        dra.year,
        arr.all_rounds,
        dra.appeared_rounds,
        arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances AS num_missed,
        -- Parse rounds into arrays for later processing (first, last missed)
        arr.all_rounds AS all_rounds_csv,
        dra.appeared_rounds AS appeared_rounds_csv
    FROM driver_year_races dra
    JOIN all_race_rounds arr ON dra.year = arr.year
    WHERE (arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances) > 0 AND (arr.total_rounds - dra.num_appearances) < 3
),
expanded_missed_rounds AS (
    -- Expand missed rounds for each driver/year
    SELECT
        dmr.driverId,
        dmr.year,
        CAST(value AS INTEGER) AS missed_round
    FROM driver_missed_ranges dmr
    JOIN (
        SELECT
            driverId,
            year,
            all_rounds_csv,
            appeared_rounds_csv,
            -- split rounds into rows: for each round in all_rounds, if not in appeared_rounds, yield it
            substr(all_rounds_csv,
                instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1,
                CASE
                    WHEN instr(substr(all_rounds_csv || ',', instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1), ',') = 0 THEN length(all_rounds_csv)
                    ELSE instr(substr(all_rounds_csv || ',', instr(all_rounds_csv, ',') * (n - 1) + 1), ',') - 1
                END
            ) AS value
        FROM driver_missed_ranges
        JOIN (
            SELECT 1 as n UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7
            UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14
            UNION SELECT 15 UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
            -- max races per year is 20 (should be enough)
        )
        WHERE n <= (length(all_rounds_csv) - length(REPLACE(all_rounds_csv, ',', ''))+1)
    ) AS rounds_split
    WHERE value NOT IN (SELECT value FROM (
        SELECT
            substr(appeared_rounds_csv,
                instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1,
                CASE
                    WHEN instr(substr(appeared_rounds_csv || ',', instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1), ',') = 0
                    THEN length(appeared_rounds_csv)
                    ELSE instr(substr(appeared_rounds_csv || ',', instr(appeared_rounds_csv, ',') * (n2 - 1) + 1), ',') - 1
                END
            ) AS value
        FROM (
            SELECT *
            FROM driver_missed_ranges AS t1
            WHERE t1.driverId = driver_missed_ranges.driverId AND t1.year = driver_missed_ranges.year
        ), (
            SELECT 1 AS n2 UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION
            SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12 UNION SELECT 13 UNION SELECT 14
            UNION SELECT 15 UNION SELECT 16 UNION SELECT 17 UNION SELECT 18 UNION SELECT 19 UNION SELECT 20
        )
        WHERE n2 <= (length(appeared_rounds_csv) - length(REPLACE(appeared_rounds_csv, ',', ''))+1)
    ))
        AND value != '' AND value IS NOT NULL
),
driver_missed_ranges_final AS (
    -- collapse to one missed range per driver/year
    SELECT
        emr.driverId,
        emr.year,
        MIN(emr.missed_round) AS first_missed_round,
        MAX(emr.missed_round) AS last_missed_round
    FROM expanded_missed_rounds emr
    GROUP BY emr.driverId, emr.year
),
edge_constructor_switch AS (
    -- For each missed range, check constructor before/after missed races
    SELECT
        dmr.driverId,
        dmr.year,
        dmr.first_missed_round,
        dmr.last_missed_round,
        -- Get constructorId right before first missed
        (
            SELECT constructorId
            FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId
              AND dra.year = dmr.year
              AND dra.round = dmr.first_missed_round - 1
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS before_constructorId,
        -- Get constructorId right after last missed
        (
            SELECT constructorId
            FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId
              AND dra.year = dmr.year
              AND dra.round = dmr.last_missed_round + 1
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS after_constructorId
    FROM driver_missed_ranges_final dmr
    WHERE
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId AND dra.year = dmr.year AND dra.round = dmr.first_missed_round - 1
        )
        AND
        EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM driver_race_appearances dra
            WHERE dra.driverId = dmr.driverId AND dra.year = dmr.year AND dra.round = dmr.last_missed_round + 1
        )
)
SELECT
    AVG(first_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_first_missed_round,
    AVG(last_missed_round * 1.0) AS avg_last_missed_round
FROM edge_constructor_switch
WHERE before_constructorId IS NOT NULL AND after_constructorId IS NOT NULL AND before_constructorId != after_constructorId;
```

```sql
    FROM order_details
),

    SELECT
        s.product_id,
        s.aisle,
        s.position,
        s.qty AS available_qty,
        i.purchase_date
    FROM stock s
    JOIN inventory i ON s.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    WHERE s.warehouse_id = 1 AND s.qty > 0
),
inv_priority AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY i.purchase_date, s.qty) AS inv_priority_order
    FROM stock s
    JOIN inventory i ON s.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    WHERE s.warehouse_id = 1 AND s.qty > 0
),
product_inv AS (
    SELECT
        s.product_id,
        s.aisle,
        s.position,
        s.qty AS available_qty,
        i.purchase_date,
        SUM(s.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY s.product_id ORDER BY i.purchase_date, s.qty ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cum_inv_qty,
        s.inventory_id
    FROM stock s
    JOIN inventory i ON s.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    WHERE s.warehouse_id = 1 AND s.qty > 0
),
assigned_picking AS (
    SELECT
        olc.product_id,
        olc.orderline_id,
        olc.ordered_qty,
        olc.cum_order_qty,
        pi.aisle,
        pi.position,
        pi.purchase_date,
        pi.available_qty,
        pi.inventory_id,
        pi.cum_inv_qty,
        -- Calculate how much needs to be picked from this inventory location for this order line
        -- This is the overlap between what is needed for this order line (up to cum_order_qty)
        -- and what is available at this inventory location (up to cum_inv_qty)
        MAX(0,
            MIN(
                pi.cum_inv_qty,
                olc.cum_order_qty
            ) - 
            MAX(
                pi.cum_inv_qty - pi.available_qty,
                olc.cum_order_qty - olc.ordered_qty
            )
        ) AS pick_qty
    FROM order_lines_cum olc
    JOIN product_inv pi ON olc.product_id = pi.product_id
    WHERE MIN(
            pi.cum_inv_qty,
            olc.cum_order_qty
        ) - 
        MAX(
            pi.cum_inv_qty - pi.available_qty,
            olc.cum_order_qty - olc.ordered_qty
        ) > 0
),
final_pick AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        orderline_id,
        aisle,
        position,
        purchase_date,
        pick_qty
    FROM assigned_picking
    WHERE pick_qty > 0
)
SELECT
    product_id,
    orderline_id,
    aisle,
    position,
    pick_qty
FROM final_pick
ORDER BY product_id, orderline_id, purchase_date, pick_qty;
```

```sql
WITH intervals AS (

  SELECT 2 UNION ALL
  SELECT 4 UNION ALL
  SELECT 6 UNION ALL
  SELECT 8 UNION ALL
  SELECT 10
),
first_terms AS (
  -- For each legislator, find their first term's start date and the state
  SELECT
    lt.legislator_id,
    MIN(lt.start_date) AS first_start_date,
    lt.state,
    l.gender
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN legislators l ON lt.legislator_id = l.id
  GROUP BY lt.legislator_id
),
retention_points AS (
  -- Build a row for each interval and legislator with snapshot dates
  SELECT
    ft.legislator_id,
    ft.state,
    ft.gender,
    i.interval_years,
    date(ft.first_start_date, printf('+%d years', i.interval_years)) as snapshot_date
  FROM first_terms ft
  CROSS JOIN intervals i
),
active_at_snapshot AS (
  -- Check if the legislator was serving on that snapshot date
  SELECT
    rp.legislator_id,
    rp.state,
    rp.gender,
    rp.interval_years,
    CASE 
      WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
        WHERE lt.legislator_id = rp.legislator_id
          AND lt.start_date <= rp.snapshot_date
          AND (lt.end_date IS NULL OR lt.end_date >= rp.snapshot_date)
      ) THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END as retained
  FROM retention_points rp
),
retention_rates AS (
  -- For each state/gender/interval, get denominator and number retained
  SELECT
    aa.state,
    aa.gender,
    aa.interval_years,
    COUNT(DISTINCT aa.legislator_id) AS total,
    SUM(aa.retained) AS retained_count,
    1.0 * SUM(aa.retained) / COUNT(DISTINCT aa.legislator_id) AS retention_rate
  FROM active_at_snapshot aa
  GROUP BY aa.state, aa.gender, aa.interval_years
),
retention_check AS (
  -- For each state/gender, require retention_rate > 0 at all 6 intervals
  SELECT
    state,
    gender
  FROM retention_rates
  WHERE retention_rate > 0
  GROUP BY state, gender
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT interval_years) = 6
),
both_genders AS (
  -- Only the states with both genders passing the filter
  SELECT
    state
  FROM retention_check
  GROUP BY state
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT gender) = 2
)
SELECT DISTINCT state
FROM both_genders
ORDER BY state;
```

```sql
WITH
-- Get minimum required inventory per product
product_min AS (
  SELECT product_id, minimum
  FROM product_minimums
),
-- December 2018 ending inventory per product
dec18_inventory AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    SUM(s.quantity) AS end_inventory
  FROM stock s
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', s.date) = '2018-12'
  GROUP BY s.product_id
),
-- Get all orders per product/month in 2019
order_outflow AS (
  SELECT
    o.product_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', ord.order_date) AS ym,
    SUM(o.quantity) AS sold_qty
  FROM orderlines o
  JOIN orders ord ON o.order_id = ord.order_id
  WHERE strftime('%Y', ord.order_date) = '2019'
  GROUP BY o.product_id, ym
),
-- Generate months in 2019
months AS (
  SELECT '2019-01' AS ym UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-02' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-03' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-05' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-08' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-09' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-11' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2019-12'
),
-- Prepare inventory calculation per product/month recursively
inventory_sim AS (
  -- Anchor: Jan 2019, start from Dec 2018 end_inventory
  SELECT
    pm.product_id,
    m.ym,
    COALESCE(d.end_inventory, 0) AS begin_inventory,
    pm.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty, 0) AS sold_qty,
    CAST(NULL AS INTEGER) AS restocked_qty,
    NULL AS end_inventory
  FROM product_min pm
  CROSS JOIN months m
  LEFT JOIN dec18_inventory d ON pm.product_id = d.product_id
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON pm.product_id = o.product_id AND m.ym = '2019-01'
  WHERE m.ym = '2019-01'

  UNION ALL

  -- Recursive: from previous month's result
  SELECT
    inv.product_id,
    m.ym,
    -- previous month's ending inventory
    inv.end_inventory,
    inv.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty, 0) AS sold_qty,
    CAST(NULL AS INTEGER) AS restocked_qty,
    NULL AS end_inventory
  FROM inventory_sim inv
  JOIN months m
    ON julianday(m.ym || '-01') = julianday(inv.ym || '-01', '+1 month')
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON inv.product_id = o.product_id AND m.ym = m.ym
)
,
-- Actually calculate restocked_amt and simulated ending inventory
rec_inventory_sim AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    ym,
    begin_inventory,
    minimum,
    sold_qty,
    -- If after outflow, ending inventory < minimum, restock by the difference
    CASE
      WHEN (begin_inventory - sold_qty) < minimum THEN minimum - (begin_inventory - sold_qty)
      ELSE 0
    END AS restocked_qty,
    -- Simulated ending inventory after restock
    (CASE
      WHEN (begin_inventory - sold_qty) < minimum THEN minimum
      ELSE (begin_inventory - sold_qty)
    END) AS end_inventory
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      -- Use LAG window to plug in previously-calced end_inventory as the begin_inventory for next month
      LAG(end_inventory) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY ym) as lagged_end_inventory
    FROM (
      -- Replace begin_inventory for months > '2019-01' with lagged value from recursive CTE
      SELECT *, 
        CASE WHEN ym = '2019-01' THEN begin_inventory ELSE NULL END as true_begin_inventory
      FROM inventory_sim
    )
  )
  -- Replace NULL begin_inventory with lagged value (from window function) for months after Jan
  -- so each month uses previous ending inventory
)
,
-- Recurse across all 12 months by joining previous month, so that begin_inventory flows
recursive_full AS (
  -- Jan 2019: Use Dec 2018 for begin_inventory
  SELECT
    pm.product_id,
    m.ym,
    COALESCE(di.end_inventory,0) AS begin_inventory,
    pm.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty,0) AS sold_qty
  FROM product_min pm
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT ym FROM months WHERE ym = '2019-01') m
  LEFT JOIN dec18_inventory di ON pm.product_id=di.product_id
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON pm.product_id = o.product_id AND o.ym=m.ym

  UNION ALL

  -- All next months
  SELECT
    rf.product_id,
    m_next.ym,
    -- begin_inventory = last month's end_inventory
    (CASE
      WHEN ((rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)<rf.minimum)
        THEN rf.minimum
        ELSE (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
    END) AS begin_inventory,
    rf.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty,0) AS sold_qty
  FROM recursive_full rf
  JOIN months m_next ON julianday(m_next.ym||'-01')=julianday(rf.ym||'-01','+1 month')
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON rf.product_id=o.product_id AND o.ym=m_next.ym
  WHERE m_next.ym>'2019-01'
),
-- Calculate post-sale, post-restock inventory per month
ending_inventory AS (
  SELECT
    rf.product_id,
    rf.ym,
    rf.begin_inventory,
    rf.sold_qty,
    rf.minimum,
    -- Add restock if under minimum; else zero
    CASE
      WHEN (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty) < rf.minimum THEN rf.minimum - (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
      ELSE 0
    END AS restocked,
    -- Ending inventory after possible restock
    CASE
      WHEN (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty) < rf.minimum THEN rf.minimum
      ELSE (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
    END AS end_inventory
  FROM recursive_full rf
)
,
abs_diff_per_month AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    ym,
    ABS(end_inventory - minimum) AS abs_diff
  FROM ending_inventory
)
,
min_diff_month AS (
  SELECT
    a.product_id,
    a.ym,
    a.abs_diff,
    -- Rank months for each product by the smallest abs_diff
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.product_id ORDER BY a.abs_diff, a.ym) as rn
  FROM abs_diff_per_month a
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  ym AS best_month,
  abs_diff
FROM min_diff_month
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY product_id;
```

```sql
  LEFT JOIN dec18_inventory d ON pm.product_id = d.product_id
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON pm.product_id = o.product_id AND m.ym = '2019-01'
  WHERE m.ym = '2019-01'

  UNION ALL

  -- Recursive: from previous month's result
  SELECT
    inv.product_id,
    m.ym,
    -- previous month's ending inventory
    inv.end_inventory,
    inv.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty, 0) AS sold_qty,
    CAST(NULL AS INTEGER) AS restocked_qty,
    NULL AS end_inventory
  FROM inventory_sim inv
  JOIN months m
    ON julianday(m.ym || '-01') = julianday(inv.ym || '-01', '+1 month')
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON inv.product_id = o.product_id AND m.ym = m.ym
)
,
-- Actually calculate restocked_amt and simulated ending inventory
rec_inventory_sim AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    ym,
    begin_inventory,
    minimum,
    sold_qty,
    -- If after outflow, ending inventory < minimum, restock by the difference
    CASE
      WHEN (begin_inventory - sold_qty) < minimum THEN minimum - (begin_inventory - sold_qty)
      ELSE 0
    END AS restocked_qty,
    -- Simulated ending inventory after restock
    (CASE
      WHEN (begin_inventory - sold_qty) < minimum THEN minimum
      ELSE (begin_inventory - sold_qty)
    END) AS end_inventory
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      -- Use LAG window to plug in previously-calced end_inventory as the begin_inventory for next month
      LAG(end_inventory) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY ym) as lagged_end_inventory
    FROM (
      -- Replace begin_inventory for months > '2019-01' with lagged value from recursive CTE
      SELECT *, 
        CASE WHEN ym = '2019-01' THEN begin_inventory ELSE NULL END as true_begin_inventory
      FROM inventory_sim
    )
  )
  -- Replace NULL begin_inventory with lagged value (from window function) for months after Jan
  -- so each month uses previous ending inventory
)
,
-- Recurse across all 12 months by joining previous month, so that begin_inventory flows
recursive_full AS (
  -- Jan 2019: Use Dec 2018 for begin_inventory
  SELECT
    pm.product_id,
    m.ym,
    COALESCE(di.end_inventory,0) AS begin_inventory,
    pm.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty,0) AS sold_qty
  FROM product_min pm
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT ym FROM months WHERE ym = '2019-01') m
  LEFT JOIN dec18_inventory di ON pm.product_id=di.product_id
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON pm.product_id = o.product_id AND o.ym=m.ym

  UNION ALL

  -- All next months
  SELECT
    rf.product_id,
    m_next.ym,
    -- begin_inventory = last month's end_inventory
    (CASE
      WHEN ((rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)<rf.minimum)
        THEN rf.minimum
        ELSE (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
    END) AS begin_inventory,
    rf.minimum,
    COALESCE(o.sold_qty,0) AS sold_qty
  FROM recursive_full rf
  JOIN months m_next ON julianday(m_next.ym||'-01')=julianday(rf.ym||'-01','+1 month')
  LEFT JOIN order_outflow o ON rf.product_id=o.product_id AND o.ym=m_next.ym
  WHERE m_next.ym>'2019-01'
),
-- Calculate post-sale, post-restock inventory per month
ending_inventory AS (
  SELECT
    rf.product_id,
    rf.ym,
    rf.begin_inventory,
    rf.sold_qty,
    rf.minimum,
    -- Add restock if under minimum; else zero
    CASE
      WHEN (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty) < rf.minimum THEN rf.minimum - (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
      ELSE 0
    END AS restocked,
    -- Ending inventory after possible restock
    CASE
      WHEN (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty) < rf.minimum THEN rf.minimum
      ELSE (rf.begin_inventory - rf.sold_qty)
    END AS end_inventory
  FROM recursive_full rf
)
,
abs_diff_per_month AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    ym,
    ABS(end_inventory - minimum) AS abs_diff
  FROM ending_inventory
)
,
min_diff_month AS (
  SELECT
    a.product_id,
    a.ym,
    a.abs_diff,
    -- Rank months for each product by the smallest abs_diff
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.product_id ORDER BY a.abs_diff, a.ym) as rn
  FROM abs_diff_per_month a
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  ym AS best_month,
  abs_diff
FROM min_diff_month
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY product_id;
```

```sql
            UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
            UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15

),

),

),

        fc.calendar_date,
        COALESCE(tx.net_txn, 0) AS net_txn

    LEFT JOIN txns tx
      ON fc.customer_id = tx.customer_id
     AND fc.calendar_date = tx.date
),

    SELECT

)

FROM monthly_max_balance
```
