            customer_id,
            MIN(txn_date) AS min_date,
            MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
        FROM signed_txn
        GROUP BY customer_id
    ) d
    JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT txn_date
        FROM signed_txn
    ) dd
    ON dd.txn_date BETWEEN d.min_date AND d.max_date
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM signed_txn) c
    WHERE d.customer_id = c.customer_id
),
per_day_txn AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        c.txn_date,
        COALESCE(SUM(s.net_amount), 0) AS net_amount
    FROM calendar c

    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.txn_date
),
running_balance AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        p.txn_date,
        SUM(p2.net_amount) AS balance
    FROM per_day_txn p
    JOIN per_day_txn p2
        ON p.customer_id = p2.customer_id

    GROUP BY p.customer_id, p.txn_date
),
rolling_30d AS (
    SELECT
        r.customer_id,
        r.txn_date,
        AVG(CASE WHEN rb.balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE rb.balance END) AS rolling_avg_30d
    FROM running_balance r
    JOIN running_balance rb
      ON r.customer_id = rb.customer_id
     AND rb.txn_date BETWEEN DATE(r.txn_date, '-29 days') AND r.txn_date
    GROUP BY r.customer_id, r.txn_date
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 30
),
date_info AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        txn_date,
        strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS ym,
        MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS baseline_ym
    FROM rolling_30d
),
rolling_with_months AS (

        di.ym,
        di.baseline_ym,

),

    GROUP BY customer_id, ym
),
filtered AS (
    SELECT

    FROM max_rolling_by_month
    WHERE ym != baseline_ym
)
SELECT
    ym AS month,
    SUM(max_rolling_avg_30d) AS summed_max_rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM filtered
GROUP BY ym
ORDER BY ym;

WITH city_inserts AS (
    SELECT
        strftime('%Y', created_at) AS year,
        strftime('%m', created_at) AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS monthly_total
    FROM cities
    WHERE (strftime('%m', created_at) IN ('04','05','06'))
      AND (strftime('%Y', created_at) IN ('2021','2022','2023'))
    GROUP BY year, month
),
months AS (
    SELECT '04' AS month UNION ALL
    SELECT '05' UNION ALL
    SELECT '06'
),
years AS (
    SELECT '2021' AS year UNION ALL
    SELECT '2022' UNION ALL
    SELECT '2023'
),
base_grid AS (
    SELECT y.year, m.month
    FROM years y
    CROSS JOIN months m
),
city_counts AS (
    SELECT
        g.year,
        g.month,
        COALESCE(ci.monthly_total, 0) AS monthly_total
    FROM base_grid g
    LEFT JOIN city_inserts ci
        ON g.year = ci.year AND g.month = ci.month
),
running_totals AS (
    SELECT
        c1.year,
        c1.month,
        c1.monthly_total,
        SUM(c2.monthly_total) AS running_total
    FROM city_counts c1
    JOIN city_counts c2
        ON c1.month = c2.month
       AND c2.year <= c1.year
    GROUP BY c1.year, c1.month, c1.monthly_total
),
final AS (
    SELECT
        rt.year,
        rt.month,

  JOIN wicket_taken w ON b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.inning_no = w.inning_no AND b.over_id = w.over_id AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id

  GROUP BY m.season, b.bowler_id

top3_bowlers AS (

WITH US_cities_sales_qtr AS (
  SELECT c.cust_city, t.calendar_quarter_desc, t.calendar_year, 
         SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_sales
  FROM sales s
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE co.country_iso_code = 'US' 
    AND t.calendar_quarter_desc IN ('Q4 2019', 'Q4 2020')
    AND s.promo_id = 0
  GROUP BY c.cust_city, t.calendar_quarter_desc, t.calendar_year
),
City_sales_growth AS (
  SELECT cust_city,
         SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_quarter_desc = 'Q4 2019' THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_19,
         SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_quarter_desc = 'Q4 2020' THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) AS sales_20
  FROM US_cities_sales_qtr
  GROUP BY cust_city
  HAVING sales_19 > 0 AND sales_20 >= 1.2 * sales_19
),
Qualified_city_sales AS (
  SELECT c.cust_city, s.prod_id, t.calendar_quarter_desc, SUM(s.amount_sold) AS prod_sales
  FROM sales s
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_iso_code = 'US'
    AND t.calendar_quarter_desc IN ('Q4 2019', 'Q4 2020')
    AND s.promo_id = 0
    AND c.cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM City_sales_growth)
  GROUP BY c.cust_city, s.prod_id, t.calendar_quarter_desc
),
Product_city_rank AS (
  SELECT prod_id, SUM(prod_sales) AS total_sales,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(prod_sales) DESC) AS rnk,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM Qualified_city_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id
),
Top_20p_products AS (
  SELECT prod_id
  FROM Product_city_rank
  WHERE rnk <= CAST(cnt * 0.2 AS INTEGER) AND total_sales > 0
),
Product_share_by_qtr AS (
  SELECT qs.prod_id, qs.calendar_quarter_desc,
         SUM(qs.prod_sales) AS top_prod_sales,
         SUM(SUM(qs.prod_sales)) OVER (PARTITION BY qs.calendar_quarter_desc) AS total_sales_in_qtr
  FROM Qualified_city_sales qs
  WHERE qs.prod_id IN (SELECT prod_id FROM Top_20p_products)
  GROUP BY qs.prod_id, qs.calendar_quarter_desc
),
Share_change AS (
  SELECT psbq.prod_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN psbq.calendar_quarter_desc = 'Q4 2019' THEN ROUND(psbq.top_prod_sales * 1.0 / psbq.total_sales_in_qtr, 5) END) AS share_2019,
         MAX(CASE WHEN psbq.calendar_quarter_desc = 'Q4 2020' THEN ROUND(psbq.top_prod_sales * 1.0 / psbq.total_sales_in_qtr, 5) END) AS share_2020
  FROM Product_share_by_qtr psbq
  GROUP BY psbq.prod_id
)

FROM Share_change sc
JOIN products p ON sc.prod_id = p.prod_id
WHERE sc.share_2019 IS NOT NULL AND sc.share_2020 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY share_change DESC

WITH city_coords AS (
  SELECT
    geolocation_state,

  FROM olist_geolocation

ordered_cities AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    LAG(avg_lat) OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, avg_lat, avg_lng
    ) AS prev_lat,
    LAG(avg_lng) OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, avg_lat, avg_lng
    ) AS prev_lng,
    LAG(geolocation_state) OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, avg_lat, avg_lng
    ) AS prev_state,
    LAG(geolocation_city) OVER (
      ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, avg_lat, avg_lng
    ) AS prev_city,
    LAG(geolocation_zip_code_prefix) OVER (

WITH june_cities AS (
  SELECT
    c.id AS city_id,
    cc.country_code,
    date(c.inserted_at) AS insert_date
  FROM cities c
  JOIN cities_countries cc ON c.id = cc.city_id

ranked_cities AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    insert_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY insert_date
    ) AS rn1,
    JULIANDAY(insert_date) -
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY insert_date
      ) AS grp
  FROM june_cities
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM ranked_cities
  GROUP BY country_code, grp
),
max_streaks AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    MAX(streak_length) AS max_streak
  FROM streaks
  GROUP BY country_code
),
top_streak AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(max_streak) AS top_length
  FROM max_streaks
)
SELECT
  ms.country_code
FROM max_streaks ms, top_streak ts
WHERE ms.max_streak = ts.top_length;

WITH female_legislators AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM legislators
  WHERE gender = 'F'
),
dec_31st_terms AS (
  SELECT lt.legislator_id, lt.state
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN female_legislators fl ON lt.legislator_id = fl.id
  WHERE (
    -- include all terms where Dec 31 between start and end
    CAST(strftime('%m-%d', COALESCE(lt.start_date, '0001-01-01')) AS TEXT) <= '12-31'
    AND CAST(strftime('%m-%d', COALESCE(lt.end_date, '9999-12-31')) AS TEXT) >= '12-31'
  )
),
first_state AS (
  SELECT lt.legislator_id, MIN(lt.start_date) AS first_start
  FROM legislators_terms lt
  JOIN female_legislators fl ON lt.legislator_id = fl.id
  GROUP BY lt.legislator_id
),
leg_first_state AS (
  SELECT f.legislator_id, t.state
  FROM first_state f
  JOIN legislators_terms t 
    ON f.legislator_id = t.legislator_id 
    AND f.first_start = t.start_date
)
SELECT d.state, COUNT(DISTINCT d.legislator_id) AS female_legislator_count
FROM dec_31st_terms d
JOIN leg_first_state lfs ON d.legislator_id = lfs.legislator_id AND d.state = lfs.state
GROUP BY d.state
ORDER BY female_legislator_count DESC
LIMIT 1;

WITH actor_years AS (
  SELECT
    M_Cast.person_id,
    strftime('%Y', Movie.release_date) AS year
  FROM M_Cast
  JOIN Movie ON M_Cast.movie_id = Movie.id
  WHERE Movie.release_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY M_Cast.person_id, year
),
actor_minmax AS (
  SELECT
    person_id,
    MIN(CAST(year AS INTEGER)) AS first_year,
    MAX(CAST(year AS INTEGER)) AS last_year
  FROM actor_years
  GROUP BY person_id
),
actor_missing_gaps AS (
  SELECT
    a.person_id,
    COUNT(1) AS max_consec_gap
  FROM actor_minmax a
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      ay.person_id,
      y AS chk_year
    FROM actor_minmax am
    JOIN generate_series(am.first_year, am.last_year, 1) AS y
      ON 1=1
    LEFT JOIN actor_years ay
      ON ay.person_id = am.person_id AND ay.year = CAST(y AS TEXT)
    WHERE ay.year IS NULL
  ) AS gaps
    ON a.person_id = gaps.person_id
  GROUP BY a.person_id
),
actor_gaps AS (
  SELECT
    a.person_id,
    a.first_year,
    a.last_year,
    -- Build a list of years and spot max consecutive gap between appearances
    (
      SELECT
        MAX(gap_len) 
      FROM (
        SELECT
          LEAD(year) OVER (ORDER BY year) - year AS gap_len
        FROM (
          SELECT
            CAST(year AS INTEGER) AS year
          FROM actor_years
          WHERE person_id = a.person_id
          UNION ALL
          SELECT a.first_year - 1
          UNION ALL
          SELECT a.last_year + 1
        )
        ORDER BY year
      ) WHERE gap_len IS NOT NULL
    ) AS max_gap
  FROM actor_minmax a
)
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM actor_gaps
WHERE max_gap <= 4
```

WITH jan_entries AS (
  SELECT
    ad.id,
    ad.city_id,
    c.country,
    DATE(ad.created_at) as entry_date
  FROM alien_data ad
  JOIN cities c ON ad.city_id = c.id

),

  SELECT
    country
  FROM jan_entries
  GROUP BY country
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT entry_date) = 9
),
country_entries AS (
  SELECT
    je.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY je.country ORDER BY je.entry_date) AS rn,
    JULIANDAY(je.entry_date) -
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY je.country ORDER BY je.entry_date) AS grp
  FROM jan_entries je
  JOIN country_9days c9 ON je.country = c9.country
  GROUP BY je.country, je.entry_date -- Make sure only unique date per country-row, if multiple entries per day, keep all for later count
),
consecutive_groups AS (
  SELECT
    country,
    grp,
    MIN(entry_date) AS start_date,
    MAX(entry_date) AS end_date,
    COUNT(DISTINCT entry_date) AS days_count
  FROM country_entries
  GROUP BY country, grp
),
longest_grp AS (
  SELECT
    country,
    grp,
    start_date,
    end_date,
    days_count
  FROM (
      SELECT *,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY days_count DESC, start_date ASC) as rnk
      FROM consecutive_groups
  )
  WHERE rnk = 1
),
country_capital AS (
  SELECT
    c9.country,
    c.id AS capital_city_id
  FROM country_9days c9
  JOIN cities c ON c.country = c9.country AND c.is_capital = 1
),
final_period_entries AS (
  SELECT

  FROM country_entries ce

WITH purchase_data AS (
    SELECT
        r.region_id,
        strftime('%Y', t.date) AS year,
        SUM(t.price_usd * t.quantity_btc) AS total_spent_usd,
        SUM(t.quantity_btc) AS total_btc_purchased
    FROM customer_transactions t
    JOIN customer_nodes n ON t.customer_id = n.customer_id
    JOIN customer_regions r ON n.region_id = r.region_id
    WHERE t.type = 'buy'
    GROUP BY r.region_id, year
),
first_years AS (
    SELECT
        region_id,
        MIN(year) AS first_year
    FROM purchase_data
    GROUP BY region_id
),
filtered_data AS (
    SELECT
        pd.region_id,
        pd.year,
        pd.total_spent_usd,
        pd.total_btc_purchased,
        pd.total_spent_usd * 1.0 / pd.total_btc_purchased AS avg_purchase_price
    FROM purchase_data pd
    JOIN first_years fy ON pd.region_id = fy.region_id
    WHERE pd.year > fy.first_year
),
region_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_purchase_price DESC) AS region_rank
    FROM filtered_data
),
annual_change AS (
    SELECT
        rd.region_id,
        rd.year,
        rd.avg_purchase_price,
        rd.region_rank,
        (rd.avg_purchase_price - lag(rd.avg_purchase_price) OVER (PARTITION BY rd.region_id ORDER BY rd.year))
            / lag(rd.avg_purchase_price) OVER (PARTITION BY rd.region_id ORDER BY rd.year)
            AS pct_change_vs_prev_year
    FROM region_ranked rd
)
SELECT 
    r.region_id,
    r.year,
    r.avg_purchase_price,
    r.region_rank,
    r.pct_change_vs_prev_year
FROM annual_change r
ORDER BY r.year, r.region_rank
```

WITH valid_wickets AS (
    SELECT
        bb.bowler_id,
        bb.match_id,
        wt.wicket_type
    FROM
        ball_by_ball bb
        JOIN wicket_taken wt ON bb.match_id = wt.match_id AND bb.inning_no = wt.inning_no AND bb.over_id = wt.over_id AND bb.ball_id = wt.ball_id
    WHERE
        wt.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out', 'retired hurt', 'obstructing the field') -- only include wickets attributed to bowlers
),
runs_conceded_per_ball AS (
    SELECT
        bb.bowler_id,
        bb.match_id,
        bb.over_id,
        bb.ball_id,
        bs.runs AS runs_off_bat
    FROM
        ball_by_ball bb
        JOIN batsman_scored bs ON bb.match_id = bs.match_id AND bb.inning_no = bs.inning_no AND bb.over_id = bs.over_id AND bb.ball_id = bs.ball_id
),
bowler_overs AS (
    SELECT
        bb.bowler_id,
        bb.match_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT (bb.over_id || '-' || bb.inning_no)) AS overs_bowled,
        COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled
    FROM
        ball_by_ball bb
        JOIN batsman_scored bs ON bb.match_id = bs.match_id AND bb.inning_no = bs.inning_no AND bb.over_id = bs.over_id AND bb.ball_id = bs.ball_id
    WHERE
        bs.runs IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        bb.bowler_id,
        bb.match_id
),
bowler_match_summary AS (
    SELECT
        rc.bowler_id,
        rc.match_id,
        SUM(rc.runs_off_bat) AS total_runs_conceded,
        bo.balls_bowled,
        COUNT(vw.wicket_type) AS wickets_taken
    FROM
        runs_conceded_per_ball rc
        JOIN bowler_overs bo ON rc.bowler_id = bo.bowler_id AND rc.match_id = bo.match_id
        LEFT JOIN valid_wickets vw ON rc.bowler_id = vw.bowler_id AND rc.match_id = vw.match_id
            AND rc.over_id = (SELECT bb2.over_id FROM ball_by_ball bb2 WHERE bb2.match_id = vw.match_id AND bb2.over_id = rc.over_id AND bb2.ball_id = rc.ball_id LIMIT 1)
            AND rc.ball_id = (SELECT bb2.ball_id FROM ball_by_ball bb2 WHERE bb2.match_id = vw.match_id AND bb2.over_id = rc.over_id AND bb2.ball_id = rc.ball_id LIMIT 1)
    GROUP BY
        rc.bowler_id,
        rc.match_id
),
best_bowling_per_match AS (
    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        MAX(wickets_taken) AS max_wickets
    FROM
        bowler_match_summary
    GROUP BY
        bowler_id
),
best_bowling_full AS (
    SELECT
        bms.bowler_id,
        bms.match_id,
        bms.wickets_taken,
        bms.total_runs_conceded,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bms.bowler_id ORDER BY bms.wickets_taken DESC, bms.total_runs_conceded ASC) AS rn
    FROM
        bowler_match_summary bms
        JOIN best_bowling_per_match bbpm
            ON bms.bowler_id = bbpm.bowler_id AND bms.wickets_taken = bbpm.max_wickets
)
SELECT
    p.player_name AS bowler_name,
    SUM(bms.wickets_taken) AS total_wickets,
    ROUND((SUM(bms.total_runs_conceded) * 6.0) / SUM(bms.balls_bowled), 2) AS economy_rate,
    CASE WHEN SUM(bms.wickets_taken) > 0
        THEN ROUND(CAST(SUM(bms.balls_bowled) AS REAL)/SUM(bms.wickets_taken), 2)
        ELSE NULL
    END AS strike_rate,
    (SELECT CAST(wickets_taken AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(total_runs_conceded AS TEXT)
        FROM best_bowling_full bbf
        WHERE bbf.bowler_id = bms.bowler_id AND bbf.rn = 1
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS best_bowling
FROM
    (
        SELECT
            bowler_id,
            SUM(total_runs_conceded) AS total_runs_conceded,
            SUM(balls_bowled) AS balls_bowled,
            SUM(wickets_taken) AS wickets_taken
        FROM
            bowler_match_summary
        GROUP BY
            bowler_id
    ) bms
    JOIN player p ON bms.bowler_id = p.player_id
GROUP BY
    bms.bowler_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY
    total_wickets DESC, economy_rate ASC, p.player_name
```

- Batting average is a measure of a batsman's performance, calculated by dividing the total number of runs scored by the number of times they have been dismissed. A higher batting average indicates a more consistent and successful batsman.
- Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Dismissals

## Strike Rate
- In batting, strike rate indicates the scoring rate of a batsman, showing the average number of runs scored per 100 balls faced. A higher strike rate reflects an aggressive and fast-scoring batsman.
- Strike Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

## Wickets Taken
- Wickets taken refers to the total number of times a bowler has successfully dismissed an opposing batsman. This statistic is a core measure of a bowler's effectiveness and impact on the game.

## Economy Rate
- Economy rate measures a bowler's efficiency by indicating the average number of runs conceded per over (6 balls) bowled. A lower economy rate shows greater control and efficiency in restricting the opposition's scoring.

- The number of times a bowler successfully dismisses a batsman in a single match.  This metric is a direct indicator of the bowler's effectiveness, showing how many players they were able to remove from play.

        bms.total_runs_conceded,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bms.bowler_id ORDER BY bms.wickets_taken DESC, bms.total_runs_conceded ASC) AS rn
    FROM
        bowler_match_summary bms
        JOIN best_bowling_per_match bbpm
            ON bms.bowler_id = bbpm.bowler_id AND bms.wickets_taken = bbpm.max_wickets
)
SELECT
    p.player_name AS bowler_name,
    SUM(bms.wickets_taken) AS total_wickets,
    ROUND((SUM(bms.total_runs_conceded) * 6.0) / SUM(bms.balls_bowled), 2) AS economy_rate,
    CASE WHEN SUM(bms.wickets_taken) > 0
        THEN ROUND(CAST(SUM(bms.balls_bowled) AS REAL)/SUM(bms.wickets_taken), 2)
        ELSE NULL
    END AS strike_rate,
    (SELECT CAST(wickets_taken AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(total_runs_conceded AS TEXT)
        FROM best_bowling_full bbf
        WHERE bbf.bowler_id = bms.bowler_id AND bbf.rn = 1
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS best_bowling
FROM
    (
        SELECT
            bowler_id,
            SUM(total_runs_conceded) AS total_runs_conceded,
            SUM(balls_bowled) AS balls_bowled,
            SUM(wickets_taken) AS wickets_taken
        FROM
            bowler_match_summary
        GROUP BY
            bowler_id
    ) bms
    JOIN player p ON bms.bowler_id = p.player_id
GROUP BY
    bms.bowler_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY
    total_wickets DESC, economy_rate ASC, p.player_name

WITH inventory_fifo AS (
  SELECT 
    i.product_id,
    i.location_id,
    i.quantity AS available_qty,
    i.purchase_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY i.purchase_date ASC, i.quantity ASC) AS fifo_rank
  FROM inventory i
),
orderlines_expanded AS (
  SELECT 
    o.id AS order_id,
    ol.product_id,
    ol.quantity AS order_qty
  FROM orderlines ol
  JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
),
match_fifo AS (
  SELECT
    oe.order_id,
    oe.product_id,
    oe.order_qty,
    inv.location_id,
    inv.available_qty,
    inv.purchase_date,
    inv.fifo_rank,
    -- The picked quantity is the overlapping amount between what the order needs and what the inventory location can provide
    CASE 
      WHEN oe.order_qty <= inv.available_qty THEN oe.order_qty
      ELSE inv.available_qty
    END AS picked_qty
  FROM orderlines_expanded oe
  JOIN inventory_fifo inv
    ON oe.product_id = inv.product_id
  -- Only consider inventory available at the time of order (optional, as there's no timestamp on the order)
)
, product_pick_stats AS (
  SELECT
    m.product_id,
    SUM(m.picked_qty) AS total_picked,
    SUM(m.order_qty) AS total_ordered
  FROM match_fifo m
  GROUP BY m.product_id
)
SELECT
  p.name AS product_name,
  CASE WHEN SUM(ps.total_ordered) > 0 THEN 
    CAST(SUM(ps.total_picked) AS FLOAT) / SUM(ps.total_ordered)
  ELSE 0
  END AS avg_pick_percentage
FROM product_pick_stats ps
JOIN products p ON ps.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY p.name;
```

WITH monthly_product_sales AS (
  SELECT
    strftime('%Y-%m', orders.order_date) AS year_month,
    products.product_id,
    SUM(orderlines.quantity) AS total_sales
  FROM
    orders
    JOIN orderlines ON orders.order_id = orderlines.order_id
    JOIN products ON orderlines.product_id = products.product_id
  WHERE
    orders.order_date >= '2016-01-01'
  GROUP BY
    products.product_id, year_month
),
-- Assign a row number to each (product_id, year_month) partition for time ordering
ordered_sales AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY year_month) AS rn
  FROM
    monthly_product_sales
),
-- For each month, calculate two overlapping 12-month moving averages
cma_calc AS (
  SELECT
    a.product_id,
    a.year_month,
    a.total_sales,
    -- First window: 5 months before (rn-5) to 6 months after (rn+6)
    (SELECT AVG(total_sales)
     FROM ordered_sales z
     WHERE z.product_id = a.product_id AND z.rn BETWEEN a.rn-5 AND a.rn+6
    ) AS cma1,
    -- Second window: 6 months before (rn-6) to 5 months after (rn+5)
    (SELECT AVG(total_sales)
     FROM ordered_sales z
     WHERE z.product_id = a.product_id AND z.rn BETWEEN a.rn-6 AND a.rn+5
    ) AS cma2,
    a.rn
  FROM ordered_sales a
),
-- Take the average of the two CMAs as the final CMA
cma_final AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    year_month,
    total_sales,
    (COALESCE(cma1,0) + COALESCE(cma2,0))/2.0 AS cma,
    rn
  FROM
    cma_calc
),
-- Calculate the sales-to-CMA ratio and restrict to months 7~30 after Jan 2016
ratio_2017 AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    SUBSTR(year_month, 1, 4) AS year,
    SUBSTR(year_month, 6, 2) AS month,
    CASE WHEN cma > 0 THEN total_sales / cma ELSE NULL END AS sales_to_cma_ratio
  FROM
    cma_final
  WHERE
    rn BETWEEN 7 AND 30
    AND year = '2017'
),
product_above_2 AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS months_with_ratio_gt_2
  FROM
    ratio_2017
  WHERE
    sales_to_cma_ratio > 2
  GROUP BY
    product_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 12  -- Must be true for all 12 months of 2017
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name
FROM
  products p
  JOIN product_above_2 pa2 ON p.product_id = pa2.product_id
ORDER BY
  p.product_id;
```

Provided benchmark documentation:

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

        test_score AS stack_test_score
    FROM model
    WHERE model_type = 'Stack'

non_stack_max AS (

    FROM model

    FROM stack_models s
    JOIN non_stack_max n
      ON s.problem_id = n.problem_id

),
sol_probs AS (

        so.problem_id,
        so.version,

    FROM solution so
),

# Flight Route Distance Calculation

## Introduction

This document describes the method used to calculate the distance between two cities for flight routes. The calculation is based on the Haversine formula, which is commonly used to find the shortest distance between two points on a sphere given their latitude and longitude. This method is especially useful for determining flight distances between airports located in different cities around the world.

## City and Coordinate Extraction

For each flight, the following data is obtained:

- **Departure city** (referred to as `from_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).
- **Arrival city** (referred to as `to_city`) and its geographical coordinates (longitude and latitude).

The coordinates are extracted as decimal values, with longitude and latitude represented in degrees. This ensures that trigonometric operations can be applied during the distance calculation.

## Haversine Formula

The Haversine formula is used to calculate the great-circle distance between two points on a sphere using their latitude and longitude. The formula is given as:

\[
d = 2r \cdot \arcsin\left(\sqrt{\sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) + \cos(\phi_1) \cdot \cos(\phi_2) \cdot \sin^2\left(\frac{\Delta \lambda}{2}\right)}\right)
\]

Where:

- \( d \) is the distance between the two points (in kilometers).
- \( r \) is the radius of the Earth (approximately 6371 km).
- \( \phi_1 \) and \( \phi_2 \) are the latitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \phi = \phi_2 - \phi_1 \) is the difference in latitudes.
- \( \lambda_1 \) and \( \lambda_2 \) are the longitudes of the departure and arrival points, respectively, in radians.
- \( \Delta \lambda = \lambda_2 - \lambda_1 \) is the difference in longitudes.

### Conversion to Radians

Since the input coordinates are in degrees, they must be converted to radians before applying the Haversine formula. This conversion is done using the formula:

\[
\text{radians} = \text{degrees} \times \frac{\pi}{180}
\]

## Symmetry of Routes

To identify unique flight routes between two cities, we standardize the order of cities in each route. Specifically, we ensure that the lexicographically smaller city name is always listed as the first city (`city1`), and the larger city is listed as the second city (`city2`). This ensures that a flight from City A to City B is treated the same as a flight from City B to City A.

## Average Route Distance

Once the distances for all flights between two cities are computed, the average distance for each city pair is calculated by summing the distances and dividing by the total number of flights between those cities:

\[
\text{Average Distance} = \frac{\sum \text{Flight Distances}}{\text{Number of Flights}}
\]

## Conclusion

This method of flight route distance calculation provides a reliable way to determine the great-circle distance between cities based on the coordinates of their respective airports. The use of the Haversine formula ensures accurate results for distances on the Earth's surface, making it ideal for aviation and travel analysis.

WITH laps_with_pos AS (
  SELECT
    lt.raceId,
    lt.driverId,
    lt.lap,
    lt.position,
    ls.status AS driver_status
  FROM lap_times lt
  LEFT JOIN results r ON lt.raceId = r.raceId AND lt.driverId = r.driverId
  LEFT JOIN status ls ON r.statusId = ls.statusId
),
overtake_candidates AS (
  -- Identify overtakes: when a driver was ahead of another on previous lap, but now behind
  SELECT
    curr.raceId,
    curr.lap,
    curr.driverId AS overtaker,
    prev.driverId AS overtaken,
    curr.position AS overtaker_pos,
    prev.position AS overtaken_pos,
    curr.driver_status AS overtaker_status,
    prev.driver_status AS overtaken_status
  FROM laps_with_pos curr
  JOIN laps_with_pos prev
    ON curr.raceId = prev.raceId
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap
    AND curr.driverId != prev.driverId
    -- Overtaker is now behind, but wasn't in the prior lap
    -- Get previous lap position for each driver
    JOIN laps_with_pos curr_prevlap
      ON curr.raceId = curr_prevlap.raceId
      AND curr.driverId = curr_prevlap.driverId
      AND curr.lap = curr_prevlap.lap + 1
    JOIN laps_with_pos prev_prevlap
      ON prev.raceId = prev_prevlap.raceId
      AND prev.driverId = prev_prevlap.driverId
      AND prev.lap = prev_prevlap.lap + 1
    -- Overtaker not behind on prior lap (ahead or equal)
    WHERE curr_prevlap.position <= prev_prevlap.position
      -- Overtaker now behind
      AND curr.position > prev.position
),
pit_entries AS (
  -- Find pit entries (drivers who pitted this lap)
  SELECT raceId, driverId, lap
  FROM pit_stops
), 
pit_exits AS (
  -- Find pit exits (drivers who pitted last lap)
  SELECT raceId, driverId, lap+1 AS lap
  FROM pit_stops
),
race_start_grid AS (
  -- Find grid positions of drivers at race start
  SELECT r.raceId, r.driverId, r.grid
  FROM results r
)
SELECT
  label,
  COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.raceId,
    o.lap,
    o.overtaker,
    o.overtaken,
    -- Classification
    CASE
      -- R: Retired this lap
      WHEN o.overtaken_status LIKE '%Retired%'
        AND (SELECT MAX(lap) FROM laps_with_pos l2 WHERE l2.raceId = o.raceId AND l2.driverId = o.overtaken) = o.lap
      THEN 'R'
      -- P: Pit entry - overtaken pitted this lap
      WHEN (SELECT 1 FROM pit_entries pe WHERE pe.raceId = o.raceId AND pe.driverId = o.overtaken AND pe.lap = o.lap) IS NOT NULL
      THEN 'P'
      -- P: Pit exit - overtaken exited last lap
      WHEN (SELECT 1 FROM pit_exits px WHERE px.raceId = o.raceId AND px.driverId = o.overtaken AND px.lap = o.lap) IS NOT NULL
      THEN 'P'
      -- S: Start - first lap, within 2 grid slots
      WHEN o.lap = 1 AND (
        SELECT ABS(g1.grid - g2.grid)
        FROM race_start_grid g1
        JOIN race_start_grid g2 ON g1.raceId = g2.raceId
        WHERE g1.raceId = o.raceId AND g1.driverId = o.overtaker AND g2.driverId = o.overtaken
      ) <= 2
      THEN 'S'
      -- T: Track
      ELSE 'T'
    END AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates o
)
GROUP BY label
ORDER BY label;
```

Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?

Provided benchmark documentation:
# Overtake Label Classification

In racing, overtakes are categorized into different states based on specific conditions, reflecting the circumstances in which the overtaking occurred. Below are the classifications and their detailed explanations:

## 1. R (Retirement) - Overtake during Retirement
An overtake is labeled as **R (Retirement)** if the overtaken driver retired on the same lap as the overtake. This indicates that the overtake occurred just before or during the overtaken driver's retirement, meaning they could no longer continue the race after that lap.

## 2. P (Pit) - Overtake related to Pit Stops
An overtake is classified as **P (Pit)** under two scenarios:
   - **Pit Entry**: If the overtake occurred while the overtaken driver was entering the pit lane, and the driver pitted on the same lap, it indicates that the overtaking happened due to the overtaken driver reducing speed to enter the pit lane.
   - **Pit Exit**: If the overtake occurred as the overtaken driver was exiting the pit lane, especially if the driver pitted on the previous lap and the time gap between the drivers was less than a typical pit stop duration. This suggests that the overtake happened while the overtaken driver was potentially at a lower speed, rejoining the race track from the pit lane.

## 3. S (Start) - Overtake at Race Start
If the overtake took place on the first lap of the race, and the two drivers were within two grid positions of each other at the start, the overtake is classified as **S (Start)**. This classification indicates that the overtake was part of the initial racing shuffle during the race's launch phase, where close position changes are common.

## 4. T (Track) - Overtake under Normal Racing Conditions
If none of the above conditions apply, the overtake is categorized as **T (Track)**, meaning it occurred during normal racing conditions on the track, without any external factors like pit stops or retirements influencing the outcome. This is the default classification for overtakes that happen during regular competition.

---

These classifications help to identify and record the context of each overtake with clarity, ensuring accurate representation of race dynamics.

WITH laps_with_pos AS (
  SELECT
    lt.raceId,
    lt.driverId,
    lt.lap,
    lt.position,
    ls.status AS driver_status
  FROM lap_times lt
  LEFT JOIN results r ON lt.raceId = r.raceId AND lt.driverId = r.driverId
  LEFT JOIN status ls ON r.statusId = ls.statusId
),
overtake_candidates AS (
  -- Identify overtakes: when a driver was ahead of another on previous lap, but now behind
  SELECT
    curr.raceId,
    curr.lap,
    curr.driverId AS overtaker,
    prev.driverId AS overtaken,
    curr.position AS overtaker_pos,
    prev.position AS overtaken_pos,
    curr.driver_status AS overtaker_status,
    prev.driver_status AS overtaken_status
  FROM laps_with_pos curr
  JOIN laps_with_pos prev
    ON curr.raceId = prev.raceId
    AND curr.lap = prev.lap
    AND curr.driverId != prev.driverId
    -- Overtaker is now behind, but wasn't in the prior lap
    -- Get previous lap position for each driver
    JOIN laps_with_pos curr_prevlap
      ON curr.raceId = curr_prevlap.raceId
      AND curr.driverId = curr_prevlap.driverId
      AND curr.lap = curr_prevlap.lap + 1
    JOIN laps_with_pos prev_prevlap
      ON prev.raceId = prev_prevlap.raceId
      AND prev.driverId = prev_prevlap.driverId
      AND prev.lap = prev_prevlap.lap + 1
    -- Overtaker not behind on prior lap (ahead or equal)
    WHERE curr_prevlap.position <= prev_prevlap.position
      -- Overtaker now behind
      AND curr.position > prev.position
),
pit_entries AS (
  -- Find pit entries (drivers who pitted this lap)
  SELECT raceId, driverId, lap
  FROM pit_stops
), 
pit_exits AS (
  -- Find pit exits (drivers who pitted last lap)
  SELECT raceId, driverId, lap+1 AS lap
  FROM pit_stops
),
race_start_grid AS (
  -- Find grid positions of drivers at race start
  SELECT r.raceId, r.driverId, r.grid
  FROM results r
)
SELECT
  label,
  COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.raceId,
    o.lap,
    o.overtaker,
    o.overtaken,
    -- Classification
    CASE
      -- R: Retired this lap
      WHEN o.overtaken_status LIKE '%Retired%'
        AND (SELECT MAX(lap) FROM laps_with_pos l2 WHERE l2.raceId = o.raceId AND l2.driverId = o.overtaken) = o.lap
      THEN 'R'
      -- P: Pit entry - overtaken pitted this lap
      WHEN (SELECT 1 FROM pit_entries pe WHERE pe.raceId = o.raceId AND pe.driverId = o.overtaken AND pe.lap = o.lap) IS NOT NULL
      THEN 'P'
      -- P: Pit exit - overtaken exited last lap
      WHEN (SELECT 1 FROM pit_exits px WHERE px.raceId = o.raceId AND px.driverId = o.overtaken AND px.lap = o.lap) IS NOT NULL
      THEN 'P'
      -- S: Start - first lap, within 2 grid slots
      WHEN o.lap = 1 AND (
        SELECT ABS(g1.grid - g2.grid)
        FROM race_start_grid g1
        JOIN race_start_grid g2 ON g1.raceId = g2.raceId
        WHERE g1.raceId = o.raceId AND g1.driverId = o.overtaker AND g2.driverId = o.overtaken
      ) <= 2
      THEN 'S'
      -- T: Track
      ELSE 'T'
    END AS label
  FROM overtake_candidates o
)
GROUP BY label
ORDER BY label;

WITH best_driver_per_constructor_year AS (
  SELECT
    cs.constructorId,
    r.year,
    MAX(ds.points) AS best_driver_points
  FROM constructor_standings cs
  JOIN driver_standings ds ON cs.raceId = ds.raceId AND cs.constructorId = ds.constructorId
  JOIN races r ON cs.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY cs.constructorId, r.year
),
team_points_per_constructor_year AS (
  SELECT
    cs.constructorId,
    r.year,
    SUM(cs.points) AS team_points
  FROM constructor_standings cs
  JOIN races r ON cs.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY cs.constructorId, r.year
),
combined_points AS (
  SELECT
    c.constructorId,
    c.year,
    b.best_driver_points,
    t.team_points,
    (b.best_driver_points + t.team_points) AS combined_points
  FROM best_driver_per_constructor_year b
  JOIN team_points_per_constructor_year t
    ON b.constructorId = t.constructorId AND b.year = t.year
  JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId = b.constructorId
)
SELECT
  co.name AS constructor_name,
  cp.year,
  cp.combined_points
FROM combined_points cp
JOIN constructors co ON cp.constructorId = co.constructorId
ORDER BY cp.combined_points DESC
LIMIT 3;

WITH over_runs AS (
    SELECT
        bb.match_id,
        bb.innings_no,
        bb.over_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) + SUM(COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs,
        MIN(bb.bowler) AS bowler -- bowler per over (first bowler found for the over)
    FROM
        ball_by_ball bb
        LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs ON bb.match_id = bs.match_id
            AND bb.innings_no = bs.innings_no
            AND bb.over_id = bs.over_id
            AND bb.ball_id = bs.ball_id
        LEFT JOIN extra_runs er ON bb.match_id = er.match_id
            AND bb.innings_no = er.innings_no
            AND bb.over_id = er.over_id
            AND bb.ball_id = er.ball_id
    GROUP BY
        bb.match_id,
        bb.innings_no,
        bb.over_id
),
max_over_per_match AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings_no,
        over_id,
        bowler,
        total_runs
    FROM (
        SELECT
            *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY match_id
                ORDER BY total_runs DESC, innings_no, over_id
            ) AS rn
        FROM over_runs
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(total_runs), 2) AS avg_highest_over_total
FROM
    max_over_per_match;
